28th pastor (Series Pastorum). No. 7/1896: the district dean demands arrears that Johann Bruckner owes the library fund from his years of service 1890, 1893 and 1894, when he was a teacher in Neustadt. No. 3396/1901: Johann Bruckner, who had been in the pastoral office of the parish of Petersdorf in the Schelk church district only since 25 August 1897, wanted as early as 1898, that is before the qualifying period had expired, to move as an ordained teacher to the elementary school in Reussen. On 29 April 1898 (no. 902/1898) it was decided that Johann Bruckner is not permitted to leave the pastoral office in Petersdorf for service as an ordained teacher in Reussen before the qualifying period expires. This was now decided in principle on 15 Nov. of this year. (ZAEKR 400/254-162.) Item 37 (1897, PP 97/16): It is to be settled what is to be done for his farewell. "Pastor Heltmann thinks that we owe it not only to the office Bruckner has held here but also to him personally to give him an honourable farewell, for he has been a man who, in the short time he has been here, has achieved a great deal; his work will certainly show in the children, and among the adults he will leave a fine memory. There is surely no one in the parish who could claim that he failed in his duty. All present agree, and the farewell ceremony is fixed as follows: 1. The presbytery gathers at 8 a.m. at the school, goes in a body to the preacher's house and takes leave of Bruckner; curator Hartel is to make the address. 2. The schoolchildren also gather at the school, are led across and line up in front of the preacher's house to say goodbye to their departing teacher; Rector Frank makes the address. 3. The mounted brotherhood, followed by the sisterhood, the schoolchildren and the presbytery, escort Bruckner to the music as far as the end of the village. 4. Having arrived there, leave is taken of him in the name of the whole parish. Speaker: Pastor Heltmann." 8 Sep 1897, item 37: "Vacancy of the post of preacher-teacher. The chairman reports that on the 6th of this month he received a letter from Johann Bruckner, pastor-teacher of Petersdorf, in which he resigns his office here as preacher-teacher and thanks the presbytery for the trust shown him. At the same time the chairman reports that Bruckner has been paid 60 florins 66 kreuzer salary for the 3rd quarter and 15 florins 21 kreuzer surplus from the leases." District no. 387/1898 of 16 Sept 1898, Großschenk, Schullerus: the filling of the preacher's post is suspended until the pastorate there, expected to fall vacant through the call of its pastor to Galt, is filled. Handover of office, record of 25 November 1910: On 25 November 1910 there act a) as commissioners Wilhelm Zintz, pastor in Jakobsdorf, and Johann Schuller, pastor in Probstdorf; b) Johann Salmen, church curator, Johann Denndorf and Michael Andrae, churchwardens, as representatives of the parish. Absent: Johann Bruckner, departing pastor of Roseln and newly elected pastor of Marpod. "Item I. The only item on the agenda is taking over the archive of the parish office and presbytery and, in connection with it, establishing the cash balance of church fund 'A', that is, of the journal kept by our brother Bruckner. 1. The archive of the parish office and presbytery is examined in detail on the basis of the inventory found, and it emerges that the contents of the archive agree exactly with the inventory, except for three savings books: a) 'Bruckner Foundation', balance 194.09 crowns; b) 'Savings book of the Evangelical church vineyard foundation', balance 61 crowns; and c) 'Parish office savings', balance 52 crowns, which are not in the inventory at all. 2. As to church fund A, the journal shows a balance of 350.05 crowns, which the senior churchwarden Joh. Denndorf takes over in cash with the instruction ... school-building fund with a balance of 783 crowns ... 3. The two register volumes III and IV and the parish office's business record are taken over by the acting pastor, Pastor Joh. Schuller of Probstdorf, whereupon the archive is locked and sealed in the presence of the church curator and the churchwardens. Pastor Schuller takes over the inventory and this record, to forward them as instructed to the Very Reverend district dean. The two savings books (a) 'In memory of dear departed', balance 446 crowns, and (b) of the Zikeli Foundation, balance 260.39 crowns, are taken over by churchwarden Denndorf, to pay for the Christmas tree from the first and to use the interest of the second for a poor orphan as the presbytery decides. Roseln, 25 November 1910. Johann Sallmen, curator; W. Zintz; Johann Denndorf; Johann Schuller, acting pastor; Michael Andree." Re district no. 142/10, 15 Nov 1910: Pastor Bruckner takes leave of the parish. He moves to Marpod on 21 Nov 1910.

"On the same day the pastor complains that some brotherhood members have had the nerve to make mischief in the street at night, rolling some burghers' building stones into the stream, throwing grindstones into the river, and so on; further, that a brotherhood officer accused them and the accused demanded proof, failing which the accuser should pay the fine they would have to pay if convicted. Since one of the accused is the headman's own son and the other a close relative of his, nobody will speak out, for fear of the headman's brutality, and the pastor finds himself obliged to hand the whole matter over to the local inspector F. Balthes for investigation. When he investigates, the accused admit their guilt and are punished."

notes: Seite.129a: „Anno 1838 den 29sten December wird das hinterlassene Vermögen des Orts=Einwohners Michael Bucholtzer unter die Witwe und unter die zwei noch unmündigen Kinder als die Tochter Sophia von 3 Jahren und unter den Sohn Michael von 1 Jahr durch das Unterfertigte Theilamt gesetzmäßig aufgetheilt, wie folget: Status Pasivus: 1. Den Joh. Röhrischen Erben auf das Obere End dem Ort zu vom ¼ land hintern Weingarten 21,4 2. Eben demselben auf ½ Viertelland über den Weg 24,8 3. Dem Mich. Frank auf ¼ land bei den Rannen 20 4. Dem Georg Frank auf die Helfte vom ¼ l. am Herbstberg 4 5. Dem Mich. Stirner auf die Graserde für der Sonhelt 7 6. Dem Joh. Geisel auf 1 theilchen aufm Wischen 6 7. Dem Mich. Frank auf ½ Grastheilchen auf der Aue 11 8. Der Maria Grek auf 1 dto eben alda 6,30 9. Dem Joh. Geisel auf 1 dto hinter der Hanfaue 8 10. Eben demselben auf 1 dto für der Großen het 7 11. Dem Mich. Gull auf 1 dto hinter der Hanfaue 2,12 12. 12 Dem Mich. Vidamnn auf 1 dto unterm Dorfe u. auf 1 theilchen im habesgraben 14,42 13. Dem Mich. Baltes auf eine ½ Wiese auf der Aue 6 14. Den Reinerischen Erben aus Schönberg 47,30 15. Dem Mayn Gligor auf ¼ land im Dalchen 10 16. Dem Moise Sollomonn auf ¼ l. über dem Weg 10 17. Dem Mich. Kößler aus Agnetheln 10 18. An Theil Gebühr 3 Summe 209,06 Jeder Gläiger wird an sein in Händen habendes Pfand angewiesen dann die Reinerische Erben aus Schönberg auch der Mich. Kößler aus Agnetheln und das Theil Gebühr an die junge Ochsen per 61 r x 30 geschätzt und gehen zur Schulden Bezahlung.“ „21 Ein zeklisches Kästchen 1 22 Ein Baumwollenes Manns Hemmet 1“

Page 129a: "In the year 1838, on 29 December, the estate of the local resident Michael Bucholtzer is lawfully divided by the undersigned estate-division office among the widow and the two children still under age, namely the daughter Sophia, aged 3, and the son Michael, aged 1, as follows. Liabilities: 1. to the heirs of Joh. Röhrich, on the upper end towards the village of the quarter-strip behind the vineyard, 21.4; 2. to the same, on half a quarter-strip across the road, 24.8; 3. to Mich. Frank, on a quarter-strip at the Rannen, 20; 4. to Georg Frank, on half of a quarter-strip on the Herbstberg, 4; 5. to Mich. Stirner, on the grassland before the Sonnhelt, 7; 6. to Joh. Geisel, on 1 small plot on the meadows, 6; 7. to Mich. Frank, on half a grass plot in the Au, 11; 8. to Maria Grek, on 1 ditto at the same place, 6.30; 9. to Joh. Geisel, on 1 ditto behind the hemp meadow, 8; 10. to the same, on 1 ditto before the Große Helt, 7; 11. to Mich. Gull, on 1 ditto behind the hemp meadow, 2.12; 12. to Mich. Vidmann, on 1 ditto below the village and on 1 small plot in the Habesgraben, 14.42; 13. to Mich. Baltes, on half a meadow in the Au, 6; 14. to the Reiner heirs of Schönberg, 47.30; 15. to Mayn Gligor, on a quarter-strip in the Dalchen, 10; 16. to Moise Sollomonn, on a quarter-strip across the road, 10; 17. to Mich. Kössler of Agnetheln, 10; 18. division fee, 3. Total 209.06. Each creditor is referred to the pledge he holds; then the Reiner heirs of Schönberg, Mich. Kössler of Agnetheln and the division fee are assigned the young oxen, valued at 61 Rhenish florins 30 kreuzer, which go to pay the debts." "21. A Székely chest: 1. 22. A man's cotton shirt: 1."

notes: 06.02.1900: Winkler Nachbarschaft beschwert sich, dass die ältesten Mitglieder der Nachbarschaft: Martin Geisel und Johann Buchholzer Kirchenväter, sowie Martin Buchholzer Organist nicht unter Kandidaten aufgenommen wurden. Vorsitzer begründet, die Kirchenväter seien vollauf beschäftigt, da Neubau des Predigerhofes bevorstehe, der Organist besitze das Freitum. 19.05.1902. Z.21 „Es liegt vor ein Gesuch des G. Baltes 16 um Verleihung der Organistenstelle. - Beschluss: Da der Organist M. Buchholzer laut Vertrag lebenslänglich angestellt und seinen Pflichten als solcher stets nachgekommen ist, wird G. Baltes mit seinem Gesuch abgewiesen, jedoch das Recht eingeräumt 3. od. 4 Sonntag zu spielen.“ 23.12.1906. Z.47 „Schließlich meldet der Vorsitzende, dass die Herren Daniel Welther in Kreisch und Johann Töpfer, Lehrer in Hermannstadt aus Anlass des Todes ihres gemeinsamen Freundes Martin Buchholzer den Betrag von 40 Kronen übergeben haben, welche den Grundstock einer Stiftung „Zum Andenken lieber Verstorbener“ bilden sollen und deren Zinsen alljährlich zur Christbescherung in der Rosler Kirche verwendet werden sollen. Zur Stärkung dieses Fonds fügt H. Johann Töpfer, Lehrer in Hermannstadt, 200 Kronen zum Andenken an seine verstorbenen lieben Eltern Michael und Sofia Töpfer bei. - Mit anderen Spenden beträgt die Stiftung nun schon 298 K., die bereits am heutigen Tage fruchtbringend angelegt wurden. Ferner spendete H. Pfarrer Johann Bruckner 170 Kronen über deren Verwendung er sich das Bestimmungsrecht vorläufig noch vorbehält. Das Presbyterium nimmt die Meldung zur Kenntnis und spricht den hochherzigen Spendern seinen Dank aus.“

6 Feb 1900: The Winkel neighbourhood complains that its oldest members, Martin Geisel and Johann Buchholzer, churchwardens, and Martin Buchholzer, organist, were not included among the candidates. The chairman explains that the churchwardens are fully occupied, since the rebuilding of the preacher's house is imminent, and that the organist is exempt. 19 May 1902, item 21: "There is a request from G. Baltes No. 16 to be given the post of organist. Decision: Since the organist M. Buchholzer is employed for life under contract and has always fulfilled his duties, G. Baltes's request is refused, but he is granted the right to play on every 3rd or 4th Sunday." 23 Dec 1906, item 47: "Finally the chairman reports that Mr Daniel Welther of Kreisch and Mr Johann Töpfer, teacher in Hermannstadt, on the death of their mutual friend Martin Buchholzer, have handed over 40 crowns to form the basis of a foundation 'In Memory of Dear Departed', the interest of which is to be used every year for the Christmas presents in the Roseln church. To strengthen this fund Mr Johann Töpfer, teacher in Hermannstadt, adds 200 crowns in memory of his late dear parents Michael and Sofia Töpfer. With other gifts the foundation now amounts to 298 crowns, which have already been profitably invested today. Further, Pastor Johann Bruckner has given 170 crowns, the use of which he reserves the right to decide for the time being. The presbytery notes the report and thanks the generous donors."

Der Plan für das Gemeindehaus wurde vom Bk genehmigt und Vorsitzer fuhr selber nach Hermannstadt um die Genehmigung beim LK zu beschleunigen. Er hat mit dem Architekten gesprochen, der etliche Bemängelungen vorgebracht hat. Er hat auch ausgeführt es sei vorteilhafter das Mauerwerk um 1 m höher und das Dach flacher zu machen. Hierüber stimmt das Presbyterium ab über den Antrag Martin Buchholzers 115: den ursprünglich Plan durchzuführen, gegen den Antrag Michael Frank 6: den Plan nach der Ansicht des Architekten zu ändern. Für den Antrag Frank stimmen 3, für den Antrag Buchholzer 7. Somit wird der Bau nach dem ursprünglichen Plan durchgeführt. 28.12.1924. 94. 95. „Nach Eröffnung der Sitzung liest Lehrer Lautner die Berichte über die drei letzten Sitzungen des Presbyteriums vor. Nach Richtigstellung einiger kleiner Ungenauigkeiten werden sie angenommen. Nur Th. Rochus 96, den es giftet, dass in der Sitzung vom 13. Dezember über das ungebührliche Betragen seines Sohnes gesprochen wurde, protestiert gegen die Sitzung und den Bericht darüber mit der Begründung, dass er in der Sitzung nicht zugegen gewesen sei. Und das wieder begründet er damit, dass er nicht mindestens einen Tag vor der Sitzung und nicht „mit einem Programm“ eingeladen worden sei, sagt aber im selben Atem, dass er an dem Tag krank gewesen sei. Er wirft dem Pfarrer vor, dass er verfassungswidrig vorgegangen sei und ihn sekkieren wolle. - Der Pfarrer weist diese Anschuldigungen zurück und hebt hervor, dass Rochus noch immer rechtzeitig eingeladen worden sei, dass aber sein Sohn - wenn er vielleicht nur dem zuliebe doch in die Sitzung gekommen wäre - auch auf der ausführlichsten schriftlichen Einladung noch nicht habe stehen können, weil er sich eben nur unmittelbar vor der Sitzung so unverschämt benommen habe. - Rochus zankt aber weiter und wirft dem Pfarrer vor, dass er seinem Sohn den Tanz heut Abend verbieten wolle. Nun versucht Knechtvater Buchholzer 115 den Pfarrer zu bewegen, den Burschen Rochus und Röhrig die Strafe zu erlassen, wenn sie um Verzeihung bäten. - Darauf erwidert der Pfarrer, dass es keine Kunst sei, um Verzeihung zu bitten, wenn man dafür eine ganze Nacht tanzen dürfe. Immerhin sei er bereit und entschlossen gewesen, die Strafe zu schenken; wenn der letzte Zugang anders verlaufen wär, hätt er’s auch getan, aber nach diesem Zugang könne er nicht. Dann schildert er, wie nach Verkündigung der Strafe auf dem Zugang der gewesene Altknecht wie ein Bolschewik die ganze Bruderschaft habe verhetzen wollen und erklärt habe, dass dann überhaupt kein Tanz sein werde, und wie er, vom Pfarrer dafür zurechtgewiesen, noch unverschämter erwidert habe, er wolle sehn, wer ihm oder einem andern am Tanzen hindern werde. Darauf fährt aber Rochus wieder auf und ist nicht zum Schweigen zu bringen. Er mischt den Herrn Jesus in die Sache und den Herrn Bischof, der es einmal schriftlich gegeben hab, dass man einzelne Knechte vom Tanz nicht ausschließen dürfe. - Der Vorsitzer fordert ihn auf, wenn er Lust habe, auch zum Bischof zu gehen, aber jetzt endlich Ruhe zu geben. - Darauf erklärt Rochus, wenn der Pfarrer das Verbot nicht zurück ziehe, dann werde sein Sohn eben trotz des Verbotes tanzen. „Ich schicke ihn, auf meine Verantwortung tanzt der Junge heute!“ - Der Vorsitzer erwidert ihm: „Dann werden Sie aber aus dem Presbyterium hinausfliegen!“ - Nun beginnt aber Rochus erstrecht zu lamentieren: Von seinem Pflug könne ihn niemand vertreiben, er gebe seinem Jungen das Brot, und allerlei anderes unsinniges Zeug - und hört nicht mehr auf. Da schreit ihn der Vorsitzer an: „Herr Rochus, schweigen Sie jetzt!“ Aber Rochus erwidert: „Ich hab das Wort“, und will weiter zanken, hört aber doch endlich auf, als ihm der Pfarrer zuruft: „Ich hab es Ihnen genommen!“ 03.05.1925. 48. (Handschrift Pauer) Buchholzer 115 stellt den Antrag, da die Umlage für die Übersiedlungskosten des Rektors noch immer nicht eingezahlt sei, der Kirchenvater solle von Haus zu Haus gehen und die Rückstände bis 10.V. eintreiben. Wird angenommen. 15.01.1933: Heinrich Lang wird zum Kirchenkassier gewählt. Es werden Buchholzer 115 zum Altkirchenvater und Hartel 10 und Bierkoch 79a mit je 4 Stimmen zum Jungkirchenvater gewählt, das Los entscheidet für Georg Hartel. Beide nehmen das Amt nicht an und danken auch als Presbyter ab. Auch die Abdankung von Martin Fleischer 15 und Stirner 46 wird zur Kenntnis genommen. 10.12.1940. Da die Schweinepreise um mehr als das doppelte gestiegen sind, werden auf Anfrage von Waagebesorger Buchholzer die Preise für Abwägen erhöht: 10 Lei für erstes und je 5 Lei für jedes weitere Tier.

The curator [moves that] half be collected as a poll tax and half as a property tax. Martin Buchholzer No. 115 moves several classes. The curator's motion is adopted by 8 votes to 6. 26 Jul 1924, item 40A: The plan for the parish hall has been approved by the district consistory, and the chairman went to Hermannstadt himself to speed up approval by the national consistory. He spoke with the architect, who raised several objections and also said it would be better to make the walls 1 m higher and the roof flatter. The presbytery then votes on the motion of Martin Buchholzer No. 115, to carry out the original plan, against that of Michael Frank No. 6, to change the plan as the architect suggests. 3 vote for Frank's motion and 7 for Buchholzer's. The building is therefore to be built to the original plan. 28 Dec 1924, items 94–95: "After opening the meeting, teacher Lautner reads the reports of the presbytery's last three meetings. After some small inaccuracies are corrected, they are approved. Only Th. Rochus No. 96, who is furious that his son's unseemly behaviour was discussed at the meeting of 13 December, protests against that meeting and its report on the grounds that he was not present. And that, in turn, he explains by saying he was not invited at least a day beforehand and 'with an agenda', yet in the same breath says he was ill that day. He accuses the pastor of acting unconstitutionally and of wanting to harass him. The pastor rejects these accusations and points out that Rochus was always invited in good time, but that his son, even if he had come to the meeting for his sake, could not have appeared on even the most detailed written invitation, since he behaved so shamelessly only just before the meeting. Rochus, however, keeps quarrelling and accuses the pastor of wanting to forbid his son to dance this evening. Brotherhood father Buchholzer No. 115 now tries to persuade the pastor to let the young men Rochus and Röhrig off their punishment if they ask forgiveness. The pastor replies that it is no great feat to ask forgiveness if you may dance all night for it. All the same, he had been ready and determined to let them off; had the last assembly gone differently, he would have done so, but after that assembly he cannot. He then describes how, after the punishment was announced at the assembly, the former senior young man (Altknecht) tried like a Bolshevik to stir up the whole brotherhood, declaring that then there would be no dance at all, and how, when the pastor rebuked him for it, he answered even more insolently that he would like to see who would stop him or anyone else from dancing. At this Rochus flares up again and cannot be silenced. He drags in the Lord Jesus and the Bishop, who had once put it in writing that individual young men may not be excluded from dancing. The chairman tells him he is welcome to go to the Bishop too, but now to be quiet at last. Rochus then declares that if the pastor does not withdraw the ban, his son will dance despite it. 'I'm sending him; on my responsibility the boy dances tonight!' The chairman replies: 'Then you'll be thrown out of the presbytery!' Now Rochus really starts to lament: no one can drive him from his plough, he gives his boy his bread, and all sorts of other nonsense, and will not stop. The chairman shouts at him: 'Mr Rochus, be quiet now!' But Rochus answers, 'I have the floor', and wants to go on quarrelling, but finally stops when the pastor calls out to him: 'I have taken it from you!'" 3 May 1925, item 48 (in Pauer's hand): Since the levy for the rector's removal costs has still not been paid in, Buchholzer No. 115 moves that the churchwarden go from house to house and collect the arrears by 10 May. Adopted. 15 Jan 1933: Heinrich Lang is elected church treasurer. Buchholzer No. 115 is elected senior churchwarden, and Hartel No. 10 and Bierkoch No. 79a receive 4 votes each for junior churchwarden; the lot falls on Georg Hartel. Both refuse the office and also resign as presbyters. The resignations of Martin Fleischer No. 15 and Stirner No. 46 are also noted. 10 Dec 1940: Since the price of pigs has more than doubled, the weighing charges are raised at the request of the scales keeper Buchholzer: 10 lei for the first animal and 5 lei for each further one.

notes: 02.12.1906: Z.37 Um die erledigte Organistenstelle haben sich beworben Johann Buchholzer 103 und Georg Balthes 116. Als Mitglieder des Wahl Skrutiniums nominiert das Presbyterium: Georg Frank 108, Johann Sallmen und Martin Balthes 104. „Die eingeleitete geheime Abstimmung ergab für Johann Buchholzer 103 fünf und für Georg Balthes 116 sechs Stimmen, wodurch Georg Balthes 116 mit einer Stimme Majorität gewählt wurde. Auf Antrag des Vorsitzenden ersucht das Presbyterium den Pfarrer und die beiden Kirchenväter den Kontrakt mit dem neu gewählten Organisten zu schließen, in welchem demselben der bisherige Organistengehalt zuerkannt werden solle, dem Presbyterium das Kündigungsrecht innerhalb drei Jahre, vom Tage der Anstellung an gerechnet, vorbehalten bleiben möge und die Verpflichtung des Organisten zur Mithilfe bei Begräbnisse zu bedingen sei. Dieser Vertrag ist dem Presbyterium in der nächsten Sitzung vorzulegen.“ 02.01.1913. 2 Adjuvanten, Joh. Buchholzer und Michael Stirner haben auf dem Pfarrhof ihre Austritt aus dem Adjuvantenchor angemeldet. Begründung: Rektor Konnerth halte die Proben nicht entsprechend. Adjuvanten Leistung sei schwach, sie schämten sich dazu zu gehören. - Rektor Konnerth weist Vorwürfe zurück. Die Proben seien schwach besucht. Wenn von 7 Adjuvanten 2-3 fehlen, könne man nicht richtig proben. Er unterrichte schon seit einem Jahr Knaben in Violinspiel. - Presbyter wünschen einen Bläserchor. Rektor verspricht einen Bläserchor abzurichten. - Presbyterium beschließt: Adjuvanten müssen ihren Austritt ein Jahr im voraus anmelden, damit entsprechend Ersatz gesucht werden kann. 10.04.1924. 27. Buchholzer 103 bittet ihm für die Zeit seines Hausbau die leere Rektorwohnung zur Verfügung zu stellen. Mit Rücksicht auf den Kindergarten, kann dies nicht gestattet werden.

2 Dec 1906, item 37: Johann Buchholzer No. 103 and Georg Balthes No. 116 have applied for the vacant post of organist. The presbytery nominates as tellers Georg Frank No. 108, Johann Sallmen and Martin Balthes No. 104. "The secret ballot gave five votes to Johann Buchholzer No. 103 and six to Georg Balthes No. 116, so that Georg Balthes No. 116 was elected by a majority of one. On the chairman's motion the presbytery asks the pastor and the two churchwardens to make the contract with the newly elected organist, granting him the previous organist's salary, reserving to the presbytery the right to give notice within three years from the day of appointment, and requiring the organist to help at funerals. This contract is to be laid before the presbytery at its next meeting." 2 Jan 1913: Two church musicians, Joh. Buchholzer and Michael Stirner, have given notice at the parsonage that they are leaving the church band (Adjuvantenchor). Their reason: Rector Konnerth does not hold rehearsals properly; the band's playing is weak and they are ashamed to belong to it. Rector Konnerth rejects the accusations. Rehearsals are poorly attended; if 2 or 3 of 7 musicians are missing, one cannot rehearse properly. He has been teaching boys the violin for a year already. The presbyters want a brass band. The rector promises to train one. The presbytery decides that church musicians must give a year's notice of leaving, so that a replacement can be found. 10 Apr 1924, item 27: Buchholzer No. 103 asks to be given the empty rector's house while his own house is being built. Because of the kindergarten this cannot be allowed.

notes: Hausnummer 16a: Bucholzer Johann, seine Frau eine geb. Stirner, seine Kinder Anna, Johann, Katharina und Martin. Der alte Bucholzer war Landwirt, hatte seinen Hof mit Pferden bestellt. Er war ein äußerst genauer Mann. Seine Frau soll ihm am Karfreitag einen Auftrag gegeben haben, er solle, bis sie aus der Kirche käme, die Eier färben, die Hälfte mit roter Farbe, dieandere mit blauer. Das Ergebnis war, Johann hatte jedes Ei zur Hälfte rot, zur Hälfte blau gefärbt. Aber die Arbeit war derart kunstvoll, daß die Kinder die Eier nicht verzehren wollten, weil sie so schön waren. Seine Frau war eine sehr bekannte Schnitterin, das heißt, sie konnte mit der Sichel besonders gut und flink umgehen. Der älteste Sohn mit dem Dorfhamen Hanzen Hartz ist als junger Bursche nach Kanada ausgewandert. Auf Anna und Katharina komme ich noch zurück. Martin blieb auf dem Hof. Seine Frau Anna Klokner, die Kinder Roland, Hedi und Erich. Martin war ein sehr musikalischer Mann, spielte die Orgel, blies das Flügelhorn bei den Adjuvanten, war auf dem Staatsgut beschäftigt und natürlich vor dem Krieg als Bauer tätig.

House No. 16a: Johann Bucholzer, his wife née Stirner, his children Anna, Johann, Katharina and Martin. Old Bucholzer was a farmer who worked his land with horses. He was an extremely precise man. On Good Friday his wife is said to have told him to dye the eggs before she got back from church, half of them red and the other half blue. The result: Johann dyed every egg half red and half blue. But the work was so artistic that the children would not eat the eggs, because they were so beautiful. His wife was a well-known reaper, that is, she was especially good and quick with the sickle. The eldest son, village name "Hanzen Hartz", emigrated to Canada as a young man. I will come back to Anna and Katharina. Martin stayed on the farm; his wife was Anna Klokner and his children Roland, Hedi and Erich. Martin was a very musical man; he played the organ and the flugelhorn in the church band, worked at the state farm and of course farmed before the war.

Z.49 „Michael Buchholzer 97 und Martin Gull 12 sind am Ostermorgen von Gendarmen nach Agnetheln eingeführt worden, weil sie das Tannenreisig zur Häuserausschmückung vom Schönberger Pfarrhof entwendet haben sollen.“ Es werden Maßnahmen besprochen. 21.11.1902: Z.50 Veruntreuung von Bruderschaftsgeldern durch die Amtsknechte: „Über Aufforderung des Vorsitzers bringt der Knechtvater Georg Frank N.108 dem Presbyterium folgendes zur Kenntnis: Er, Knechtvater sei auf den letzten Zugang der Bruderschaft nur kurz vor dem Vesperläuten gerufen worden. Da habe Baltes Joh. N.109 im Namen der Bruderschaft die Erklärung abgegeben: Die Amtsknechte hätten, wie sich aus einem aufliegenden Verzeichnisse beweisen lasse, die auf dem letzten Zugang eingegangenen Strafgelder nur teilweise in die Bruderschaftskasse abgeführt, einen beträchtlichen Teil derselben aber unterschlagen. Die Bruderschaft, ausgenommen Michael Buchholzer N.97, Altknecht, und Martin Salmen N.64 Jungaltknecht, erkläre ferner, dass sie ehe diese Angelegenheit untersucht und die Schuldigen bestraft würden, keine Strafgelder mehr in die Bruderschaftskasse zahle. Diese Angelegenheit wird vom Presbyterium mit bedauern zur Kenntnis genommen und beschlussmäßig dahin geordnet: Nächsten Sonntag nach beendigtem Predigtgottesdienst soll die Bruderschaft im Beisein des Presbyteriums einem Verhör unterzogen werden. Hinsichtlich der Bestrafung der Amtsknechte bei nachgewiesener Veruntreuung der Bruderschaftsgelder werden folgende Anträge eingebracht: Antrag Hartel 106: Die Amtsknechte Buchholzer 97 und Sallmen N.64 sollen abgesetzt werden und den fehlenden Betrag ersetzen. Antrag Fleischer 66: Der vorliegende Fall soll als warnendes Beispiel für die spätern Amtsknechte auf dem Schlussblatt der Artikel eingetragen und die Schuldigen zum vierfachen Ersatz des fehlenden Betrages verpflichtet werden. - 12.03.1939. „Vorsitzer erinnert des Presbyterium daran, dass seit längerer Zeit schon, besonders aber seit dem 12. Februar in der Gemeinde sehr viel über ein Verhältnis von Presbyter Michael Buchholzer 67 zu Frau Klockner 90 geredet werde. Er sagt, dass es im Interesse beider liege hier Klarheit zu schaffen: Sei etwas an der Sache, müsse gegen Buchholzer 67 die Disziplinaranzeige erstattet werden, sei nichts an der Sache, müsse es im Interesse von Herrn Buchholzer 67 liegen, durch unparteiische Klarheit zu schaffen. Damit sich das Presbyterium in der Angelegenheit orientieren könne, schlägt Vorsitzender vor, eine Kommission mit der Voruntersuchung zu betrauen. Alle anwesenden Presbyter wissen, dass in dieser Sache viel geredet wird, weshalb der Vorschlag vom Vorsitzenden einstimmig zum Beschluss erhoben wird. In die Kommission werden ernannt: Vorsitzender Adolf Lutsch, Pfr., als Schriftführer Heinrich Lang, Lehrer, Kurator Martin Fleischer und Michael Stirner 60 als Beisitzer.“ 16.04.1939. „Betreffend dem Verhältnis von Herrn Buchholzer 67 mit Frau Klockner 90 berichtet Vorsitzender, dass eine Untersuchung in dieser Angelegenheit stattgefunden habe. Herr Buchholzer 67 habe in einer schriftlichen Erklärung das Mandat als Presbyter niedergelegt. Darauf hin hätte die Kommission von einer weiteren Untersuchung abgesehen. Es bestehe die Möglichkeit die ganze Angelegenheit der nächst höheren Instanz zur weiteren Untersuchung zu übergeben, oder die Erklärung vom Genannten zur Kenntnis zu nehmen und somit die Angelegenheit als erledigt anzusehen. Das Presbyterium sieht von einer Weiterleitung dieser Angelegenheit ab, und betrachtet die Angelegenheit auf Grund der Erklärung von Herrn Buchholzer 67 von seiner Seit als erledigt an.“

3 Apr 1899, item 49: "Michael Buchholzer No. 97 and Martin Gull No. 12 were taken to Agnetheln by gendarmes on Easter morning because they are alleged to have taken fir branches for decorating the houses from the Schönberg parsonage." Measures are discussed. 21 Nov 1902, item 50: Embezzlement of brotherhood money by the brotherhood officers. "At the chairman's request, brotherhood father Georg Frank No. 108 informs the presbytery as follows: at the brotherhood's last assembly he was called only shortly before the ringing for Vespers. Johann Baltes No. 109 then declared in the name of the brotherhood that the officers, as could be proved from a list on the table, had paid only part of the fines collected at the last assembly into the brotherhood's funds and had embezzled a considerable part. The brotherhood, except Michael Buchholzer No. 97, senior officer (Altknecht), and Martin Salmen No. 64, junior senior officer, further declared that until this matter was investigated and the guilty punished, they would pay no more fines into the brotherhood funds. The presbytery notes this matter with regret and decides as follows: next Sunday after the preaching service the brotherhood is to be questioned in the presence of the presbytery. As to punishing the officers if embezzlement of brotherhood money is proved, the following motions are made. Hartel No. 106: the officers Buchholzer No. 97 and Sallmen No. 64 are to be removed and must make good the missing sum. Fleischer No. 66: the present case is to be entered on the final page of the articles as a warning to later officers, and the guilty are to repay four times the missing sum." 12 Mar 1939: "The chairman reminds the presbytery that for some time now, but especially since 12 February, there has been a great deal of talk in the village about an affair between presbyter Michael Buchholzer No. 67 and Mrs Klockner No. 90. He says it is in the interest of both to clear this up: if there is something in it, a disciplinary complaint must be brought against Buchholzer No. 67; if there is nothing in it, it must be in Mr Buchholzer's own interest to have it cleared up impartially. So that the presbytery can inform itself on the matter, the chairman proposes that a committee be entrusted with a preliminary inquiry. All the presbyters present know that there is much talk about this, so the chairman's proposal is adopted unanimously. Appointed to the committee: the chairman, Pastor Adolf Lutsch; as secretary Heinrich Lang, teacher; and curator Martin Fleischer and Michael Stirner No. 60 as assessors." 16 Apr 1939: "Concerning the affair of Mr Buchholzer No. 67 with Mrs Klockner No. 90, the chairman reports that an inquiry into the matter has taken place. Mr Buchholzer No. 67 has resigned his mandate as presbyter in a written statement. The committee therefore refrained from further inquiry. It would be possible to pass the whole matter to the next higher authority for further investigation, or to note the statement and so regard the matter as closed. The presbytery decides not to pass the matter on, and regards it as closed on its part on the strength of Mr Buchholzer's statement."

Kirchengemeinde A.B. in Roseln einerseits und dem Organisten Martin Buchholzer H.No.l6 andererseits wird nachstehender Vertrag geschlossen: Der oben Genannte wird als Organist an der evang. Der Organist ist gehalten bei jeder Art von Gottesdienst das Orgelspiel in gewissenhafter Weise zu besorgen. 2. 1m Falle der Behinderung, sei sie welcher Art immer, hat er auf eigene Kosten und Verantwortung einen Orgelspieler zu stellen. 3.Ortsabwesenheit an Tagen da Gottesdienst ist u. Mit dem Organisten Buchholzer hat die Verhandlung ergeben, dass er mit dem Grund, den er heuer benützt hat zufrieden ist, wenn die Kirchengemeinde ihm die Steuer und abzuliefernde „cota“ ersetzt. Das Presbyterium beschließt einstimmig darauf einzugehen. (Wird dahingehend verbessert: mit 7 gegen 1 Stimme.) 04.04.1948: 22. „nach längeren Verhandlungen stellt das Presbyterium den Organisten Buchholzer auch für das eben beginnende Rechnungsjahr an. Es sichert ihm ein Monatsgehalt von 400 Lei und Freiheit von Kirchen- und Nachbarschaftsarbeit zu.“ [Keinen Boden mehr?] 30.01.1949: 4. Bk-Erlass Z.556/1948 betr. beschleunigte Einhebung und Abfuhr der Taxen für Bezirksgemeinde. Bericht über geldliche Lage der Kirchengemeinde und Gehaltsrückstände des Vorsitzers. Als Pfarrer und Lehrer stehen ihm 52.011 Lei zu, Rektor Reiner noch 3.659, Organist Buchholzer 1.200, Gesamtgemeinde 35.071, Bezirk 5.343 = zusammen 97.820 Lei. Ohne Schulden müssten bis 31.3. aufgebracht werden 43.174 Lei, einzukassieren wären 125.000 Lei, die nicht zu erträumen sind, aber doch noch einen Fehlbetrag von 15.794 Lei ergäben. „So rächt es sich, wenn man bei Aufstellung des Voranschlages bewusst mit zu großen Einnahmen und zu kleinen Ausgaben rechnet, um ihn leichter annehmen zu lassen, und im Lauf des Jahres nicht tatkräftig genug die Taxen einhebt.“ 30.12.1949. 30. „In langen Verhandlungen mit dem Organisten Buchholzer wird sein Lohn auf 450 Lei monatlich erhöht … falls er keine Lebensmittel und Kleiderkarte bekommt, wird sein Lohn auf 500 Lei erhöht.“ 30.12.1956: (anwesend alle, + Martin Buchholzer, Organist) Z.57/1956 1.) Barentlohnung des Organisten steigt von 60 auf monatlich 70 Lei. 2.) „Organist behält das Recht auf dem Friedhof unentgeltlich zu mähen.“ 3.) „Von Nachbarschaftsleistungen ist er zwar nicht befreit, doch wird ihm ein aus der Vergangenheit herrührender strittiger Betrag, die die Obere Nachbarschaft von ihm fordert, in der einmaligen Höhe von 32 Lei aus Kirchenmitteln vergütet.“ 04.02.1959. Organist wird von 70 auf 80 Lei monatlich erhöht. 25.02.1959: Organist Martin Buchholzer ist in Streik getreten, weil seine Forderungen nicht ganz erfüllt wurden. Es soll in Umgemeinden und in Roseln nach Ersatz gesucht werden, Jugendliche, die Orgelspiel erlernen können. 03.01.1960: Organisten Buchholzer werden die 100.- Lei monatlich gewährt (aber andere Form). VIII. 11.12.1964: P.35 Organistenlohn wird auf eine Viertelnorm festgesetzt und ist unter beide Organisten zu teilen. XII: 07.12.1966: Erhöhung Organistenlohn. (je 75.- Lei pro Monat).

Occupations: farmer in Roseln; in 1951 track worker on the state railway in Roseln. Residence: No. 16 in Roseln. 30 Jun 1940: Contract with the organist Martin Buchholzer. Organist in Roseln: "The young man Martin Buchholzer No. 16, having completed an organists' course, is appointed organist of the parish for one year. The pay due to an organist, however, goes to teacher Lang, because he [Buchholzer] is not yet able to accompany the service alone." 1 Nov 1980 [PP 22/135], item 18: "Organist Martin Buchholzer No. 198 has submitted his letter of resignation (see item 127), because he too is emigrating to the Federal Republic of Germany, and has already held a farewell with the presbytery, church band and church choir. He has recommended Michael Geisel junior, No. 217, as his successor, whom he has been preparing and introducing for months. This recommendation and his past efforts are gratefully acknowledged, and the contract with Michael Geisel is discussed. It is decided that Michael Geisel junior, No. 217, is to be appointed organist from 1 December 1980 on the same terms as his predecessor (see items 126, 127)." Martin Buchholzer No. 16, parish no. 23/1940 (pencil note: "Has in fact served as organist since 1939"). Second World War: called up since the end of June 1942. He is replaced by the organist of Jakobsdorf, who asks 300 lei a Sunday. The organist's mother provides meals and, in bad weather, the wagon to the station. The parish pays half the cash cost of the deputy. [Serving as organist filled this life.] Extracts from letters and greeting cards sent by Roseln soldiers to Pastor Lutsch and read out in church: Martin Buchholzer, house No. 16, writes a fine letter from Narva. He was in the field hospital for a short time with frozen toes and an abscess on his thumb, and can then go back to the front line. He sends his warmest greetings to the whole parish, the young people and all his comrades at the front. [Pastor's reply:] "Dear soldiers! I thank you all for the greetings and good wishes you have sent me and my family in your letters. We wish you all the best too. Stay well, and God be with you! Adolf Lutsch." Contract: The following contract is concluded between the Evangelical parish A.B. in Roseln on the one part and the organist Martin Buchholzer, house No. 16, on the other: the above-named is appointed organist of the Evangelical church on the following conditions. Duties: 1. The organist must play the organ conscientiously at every kind of service. 2. If he is prevented, for whatever reason, he must provide an organist at his own cost and responsibility. 3. Absence from the village on days with a service, and staying away from the service, is permitted only with the pastor's leave, even if the deputy mentioned in point 2 is provided. 4. The organist must take an exemplary part in the church band, on the conditions that apply to it. 5. In case of breach of duty the presbytery is entitled to recoup itself from the yield of the land, or to apply this as a sanction. Rights: 1. As pay for the services rendered to the church, the church guarantees the organist the free use of the plot of about 8 yokes in the "Honfeld" known as the organist's land. In the event of any change in property, the church shall not be hindered and shall have the right to compensate the organist with land of equal value elsewhere. 2. The organist is exempt from all church labour, except work that occurs as a one-off and counts as a levy. 3. The benefits given by the civil commune (wood, exemption from labour) are guaranteed to the organist by the church only conditionally, that is, if they lapse against its will it is not obliged to make them good. Final section: 1. Organist Martin Buchholzer is appointed for life. Each party, however, has the right to withdraw from this contract by giving notice; the notice period is two years and can be shortened only with the consent of both parties. 2. In any disputes that may arise, both parties submit, excluding any further legal remedy, to the arbitration of the Evangelical district consistory A.B. of Schenk. Roseln, 1 July 1940. The Evangelical presbytery A.B.: Adolf Lutsch, chairman; W. Hermann, secretary. Organist: Martin Buchholzer. Guardian of the organist: Anna Buchholzer. Witnesses: M. Fleischer No. 15, E. Fleischer No. 15. 24 Aug 1947, item 64: The district consistory, under no. 202/1947, instructs the presbytery to negotiate the matter with organist Buchholzer again and reach an amicable agreement with him. 31 Aug 1947, item 71: The negotiation with organist Buchholzer has shown that he is satisfied with the land he used this year, if the parish pays his tax and the quota (cota) he has to deliver. The presbytery decides unanimously to agree. (Corrected to: by 7 votes to 1.) 4 Apr 1948, item 22: "After lengthy negotiations the presbytery also appoints organist Buchholzer for the financial year now beginning. It guarantees him a monthly salary of 400 lei and exemption from church and neighbourhood labour." [No land any more?] 30 Jan 1949, item 4: District consistory decree no. 556/1948 on speeding up the collection and payment of fees for the district. Report on the parish's finances and the chairman's salary arrears. As pastor and teacher he is owed 52,011 lei, Rector Reiner still 3,659, organist Buchholzer 1,200, the wider church 35,071, the district 5,343, in all 97,820 lei. Leaving debts aside, 43,174 lei would have to be raised by 31 March; 125,000 lei would have to be collected, which is beyond our dreams, and even that would leave a shortfall of 15,794 lei. "This is the revenge for knowingly reckoning with too much income and too little expenditure when drawing up the budget, to get it passed more easily, and then not collecting the fees energetically enough during the year." 30 Dec 1949, item 30: "After long negotiations with organist Buchholzer his pay is raised to 450 lei a month ... if he does not receive a food and clothing ration card, his pay is raised to 500 lei." 30 Dec 1956 (all present, plus Martin Buchholzer, organist), no. 57/1956: 1.) The organist's cash pay rises from 60 to 70 lei a month. 2.) "The organist keeps the right to mow the cemetery free of charge." 3.) "He is not exempt from neighbourhood duties, but a disputed sum dating from the past, which the upper neighbourhood claims from him, is reimbursed to him once from church funds, to the amount of 32 lei." 4 Feb 1959: The organist's pay is raised from 70 to 80 lei a month. 25 Feb 1959: Organist Martin Buchholzer has gone on strike because his demands were not met in full. A replacement is to be sought in the surrounding villages and in Roseln: young people who can learn to play the organ. 3 Jan 1960: Organist Buchholzer is granted the 100 lei a month (but in another form). VIII. 11 Dec 1964, p.35: The organist's pay is set at a quarter-norm and is to be shared between the two organists. XII. 7 Dec 1966: Increase of the organist's pay (75 lei a month each).

"Johann Burbrieger. 'Man, it is the old covenant: you must die.' As the late honourable man Joh. Burbrieger, burgher and inhabitant of our royal village of Roseln, had to learn in deed and in truth. Accordingly the deeply grieving widow asked the estate-division officers of that time, Joh. Fleischer senior and Simon Geissel junior, to make a settlement for her and her two children over the half-share left by their father, which they did according to the statutes of the land and in good conscience. Done in the year 1751, on 6 January. The mother's share: first she was given a vineyard below the Duirefisch next to Georg Weber's widow and Georg Buholzer; also half a yoke of land below the Loy next to Mart. Bierkoch; before the Alutern field, half a yoke next to Michl. Schuster, for interest. Vineyards: first, a vineyard above the village next to Lucas Schuster; in the Sandkell above the ridge, one next to Joh. Bucholsser; in the Schrewen, one next to Mich. Baldes. Arable land, Grund field: first, below the Kleine Feld, half a yoke next to Michl. Franck; before the Sonnheld, half a yoke next to Michl. Zucker; in the Hanvold, half a yoke next to Joh. Franck; in the great Au, a strip of 5 paces next to Chrestel ...; before the Schrewen Berg, half a yoke next to Jacob Orendy. Probstdorf field: first, in the Krumme Fuhrling, half a yoke next to Joh. Bucholzer; on the Loyen [?], three quarters of a strip next to Lucas Schuster; in the Leichen Weingarten, three quarters of a strip next to Jacob Orend. Agnetheln field: first, by the Wannen, half a yoke next to her son; by St Kloss, half a yoke next to Joh. Bucholzer; above the village, half a yoke next to her son; in the Lawass, half a yoke next to Mich. Zucker; on the Wisgen, half a yoke next to Joh. Wagner. Iron and wood: an iron tongs [?], a spit and a ..., a ??; a chest of 12 bushels; also a cabbage tub and a tub; a cask of 18 Urn and another of 16 Urn, another of 12 Urn. Military-service (Heerfahrt) days: 306. Johann's share: first, from his father's half-share he is given two oxen and half a yoke before the Scheuren Berg next to Mich. Franck, for which he is to be bound to provide for his mother until her death, both with carting of wood and to the mill and by cultivating half a yoke in each field for her; in the autumn he is to let her share [the harvest]. Also he was given half a yoke below the Kleine Feld next to Joh. Töpfer, which is [pledged] for interest at ... florins 50 denars; also a young stallion foal. Vineyards: first, in the Schrewen, a vineyard next to Catharina's vineyard; below the village a small vineyard next to Mart. Bierkoch (given as a morning gift, N.B.); also one above the village below the Winn [?] next to Joh. Fleischer; and again one below the village next to Jacob Orend. Arable, Grund field: first, below the Kleine Held, half a yoke next to his mother; at the Steinreg, half a yoke next to Mich. Wiemann; in the great Au, a strip of 10 paces next to Mich. Franck; in the Handvolld, three quarters of a strip in the Haag; they are to share the fruit of the tree as long as the ... lives, but afterwards the tree shall belong to whoever gets the land. Before the Wiederrann [?], half a yoke next to Joh. Schmied. Probstdorf field: first, by the pond, a yoke next to Mart. Binder; on the gardens, half a yoke next to Simon Fleischer; by the vineyards, half a yoke next to Joh. Wagner. Agnetheln field: first, by the Rannen, half a yoke next to his sister; by St Kloss, half a yoke next to his mother; above the village, half a yoke next to Mich. Lurtz; on the Hundsrück, half a yoke next to Georg Bucholzer. Iron and wood: he was given a chain, a drill and a frying pan; a 40-Kof [cask], and another 40-Kof. Military-service days: 306. Catharina's share: first she was given a horse [?], half a yoke of meadow in the Baussner Loch next to Joh. Töpfer, which is pledged to Mich. Kentz in Abtsdorf for 5 florins. Vineyards: first, in the Schrewen, a vineyard next to Mert. Geissel; in the Hamdvold, one on the ridge next to And. Bucholzer; above the village, one next to Joh. Töpfer. Arable, Grund field: first, below the Kleine Held, half a yoke next to Michael Boldes; before the Sonnhelf, a yoke next to Joh. Bucholzer; on the Knallen Hüle, a strip of 10 paces next to Mert. Binder; on the Wotsen Weg, half a yoke next to Joh. Stäntzel; before the Sonnheld, half a yoke next to Joh. Zintz; behind the Schrewen Berg, three quarters of a strip next to the common land. Probstdorf field: first, on the 60 yokes, three quarters of a strip next to Mart. Binder; in the Leichen Weingärten, half a yoke next to Mich. Baldes (weaver); across the road, one and a half quarter-strips next to Joh. Binder. Agnetheln field: first, by the Rannen, half a yoke next to the common land; by St Kloss, half a yoke next to her brother; on the Herbst Berg, half a yoke next to Thomm. 14th pastor (Series Pastorum). (Arz says he was born in Roseln, but does not know where he came to Rosch from, nor where he went.) He was not the 14th pastor of Roseln; according to the church account book, Helner followed directly after Deidricius. –1682: 14th pastor Johann Cunradi, a native of Roseln, died 1683 in Roseln. He is attested in Roseln from 1658. His son Georg was the 7th pastor in Rosch, 1718–1747. His daughter Anna married the pastor's son Christian Phlegner in Reps on 14 Nov 1716. ("Conrad" in Arz.) E. Wagner no. 1485. Was he also pastor in Rosch?
