(School handover) "The chairman reads out in full the circular of the most worshipful Regional Consistory LK Z.K.2820/1941 concerning the handover of the school and educational system under the Evangelical Church A.B. in Romania to the German Ethnic Group in Romania, as well as the circular of the same authority under LKZ.K2820/1941 concerning the draft resolution of the Regional Consistory for the handover of the German schools and educational institutions of the Church to the German Ethnic Group. - Following this he opens the decrees for discussion. As no one asks to speak, he remarks that the main question is probably whether the property serving the school should be transferred into the ownership of the Ethnic Group or not. Thereupon churchwarden and local leader Michael Frank No. 18 moves: The entire property of our church serving the school, both movable and immovable, shall be transferred free of charge into the ownership of the German Ethnic Group. The chairman opens the motion for discussion. No one asks to speak. Thereupon the chairman, so as not to be exposed to distortions and misinterpretations, reads out the following word for word: 'Worshipful presbytery! Through the Ethnic Group's demand for the immediate handover of our Evangelical German school system and the church property serving it, we are faced with a question of perhaps greater importance than any since our Church has existed. For the consequences arising from it cannot today be estimated or weighed by anyone. A few days ago a representative of the Ethnic Group spoke in the school before a group of men about Decree-Law No. 977 of 7 Nov 1941, and it was expressly said that the new type of German school to be created on the basis of this law shows no progress whatever compared with the state laws of this kind we had so far, but in some respects means a deterioration. Nevertheless the Church can declare itself ready to hand over the Evangelical German school system to the Ethnic Group, especially as it must itself be concerned that all children of the German people enjoy a uniform German, and indeed National Socialist, education. The school does not belong to the Church's most essential task. What is entrusted to the Church under all circumstances is this: the proclamation of the good news of Jesus Christ! If it has nevertheless maintained the German school with great faithfulness and often to the point of self-sacrifice, this happened because no one else was found who would have done it, and because it knew that it had to be done. I myself, in the 12 years of my ministry so far, have worked for the preservation of our German school to the limit of my capacity and have achieved and sacrificed more for it than anyone in our community. I did so because I am attached to my German people with all the love of which a person is capable. If someone now comes today and says: I can run the German school system better than the Church, - then the Church can only be glad of it. It also has nothing to lose by it, only to gain. For now it can turn with all its strength to its real task: proclamation, that task which until now it has all too often neglected for the sake of the other. I owe it to the community, and my conscience and my oath of office oblige me, to take a position on the manner and the way in which the handover is to take place. If I did not do so, the gravest reproaches might one day rightly be made against me. I do not wish thereby to force a decision in my favour; nor do I wish to influence anyone; least of all do I wish to do what the church people themselves do not want. Nor do I wish to speak of the possibilities that will open up for the school in the future, because I know myself to be fully released from responsibility for it from the moment of the handover. But I must speak plainly of the dangers that arise for the continued existence of our Church. The draft resolution of the Regional Consistory is so unclear and so general that the worst disputes must arise in the division between church and school. We are supposed to resolve, and we do not know what we are supposed to resolve. We are supposed to issue a blank cheque, on the basis of which a commission coming from outside the community and not bound to the church decides what belongs to the school and what does not. There is no part of the church property that could not be viewed from this angle. For two full weeks I sought an answer to these questions, day and night, and found none: Why is the game not played with cards fully on the table? Why must such an important matter be decided so quickly, overnight, when it has been through the centuries as it is today? Why is it done in a form that wounds the honour of the Church? Why are no unambiguous, clear, mutual contracts concluded? It is without doubt true that what is at stake is whether the Evangelical Christian good news is still to be proclaimed among us or not. Not because the Church could not do this without the school; that it can do it even better without it I said above. But what is at stake is the material foundation and the material existence of the Church. Without these it simply cannot exist in this given world. Of course, the Lord of the Church builds His Church as He wills; we need not help Him with that. But if it is to remain a visible Church, and only then can it do its service to our German people, it cannot do without an earthly foundation. It is my belief that the Church must never act against the interests of the German people. If it did, I would resign my service in it. But I am also convinced that our people need its service as a contribution to realising their eternal existence. It is a word as frivolous as it is dangerous when it is said: The point now is that it is no longer the pastor who gives orders, but others. Whoever operates with this has truly not understood the signs of the times and does his people and his Church a poor service. I confess here too that I have never felt giving orders to be a joy, but always a burden which I would gladly have given up. If I nevertheless did not do so, it was because no one was found for it and because I knew myself obliged towards the community. I need only recall the church work: until 1935 I gave no orders whatever in it, but let the churchwardens manage as they saw fit; it was after all their task. Was the result not that we made no progress with the school building, because almost no one came to work? I took the matter in hand not to give orders but to serve the community. It is exactly the same everywhere. It is said: We are after all still the same people! That this unfortunately is no longer true has been shown by the agitation over this important question. And if that is so, - why is the Church so mistrusted? Does anyone seriously believe that the Church wants to hinder or harm the school, when it has done so infinitely much for it until now? Before the World War the Orthodox Church had exactly the same denominational schools as we did. When after the war the Romanian state took over these schools, the buildings were left to it and the state paid rent for its schools. Until now it has occurred to no one to reproach the Orthodox Church for this, least of all for not being national. The Catholic Church also maintains a number of German schools, in the Banat and in Transylvania. Will it also place its property unconditionally at the disposal of the Ethnic Group? What I have heard of it so far suggests the answer is no. But if the Evangelical Church alone, with its large school property, contributes to the establishment of the German national school, that is an enormous weakening of the Evangelical Church compared with the Catholic Church. Would it not be fairer if all of us, Evangelicals and Catholics, contributed equally to the German national school? The Church and its proclamation in danger! Worshipful presbytery, I have often asked myself whether that is true. Judge for yourselves the following: Last Sunday I was called to a meeting of office-holders at which two gentlemen from Agnetheln were present. There we were told: This year the children's Christmas gift-giving is to be carried out by the N.S.V. [National Socialist People's Welfare]. The celebration to be held on that occasion takes place as before, in the church at the same time as was customary. The exact programme of this celebration will be sent to the local group leadership by the district leadership. Likewise the address to be given at this celebration will be sent. If the pastor declares himself willing to give this and no other address, he gives it; if not, the rector gives it. - As I learned further by word of mouth, no Christian songs may be sung on that occasion, not even the song "Silent night, holy night". To me it follows with great clarity: on Christmas Eve the parish is to be deprived of its Christian service and it is to be replaced by a celebration which at the least has nothing to do with Christianity. Let none of you be influenced or even forced in his decision. Let each decide as he can answer for it before his conscience, before his children and before his Lord God, and as he can reconcile it with his oath on being installed in his office as presbyter. The Bishop has always stood up for freedom of conscience; as free Evangelical and German people we wish to follow it!' Following this the chairman makes the following counter-motion: '1. The Evangelical parish of Roseln hands over with immediate effect the pedagogical, disciplinary and administrative management of the entire German school and educational system hitherto maintained and managed by it to the German Ethnic Group in Romania, with all the rights and duties arising therefrom. 2. The Ethnic Group takes over the teaching staff hitherto in the service of the parish of Roseln, preserving their acquired financial rights. 3. No costs of any kind, nor financial claims of third parties, may accrue to the parish of Roseln as a result of the handover of the school system with all its consequences. For this reason all teaching staff hitherto in its service must resign their posts with the parish upon the handover. The salaries of the teaching staff until 30 March 1942 will be paid by the parish of Roseln according to the instructions to be given by the most worshipful Regional Consistory. 4. In order to be able to take over the running of the school, the parish of Roseln places the following movable and immovable property at the disposal of the German Ethnic Group under the following conditions. a. The movable property consists of the furnishings and teaching materials of the school. b. The immovable property of the school includes: 1. the school building built in 1936 together with the teacher's residence and the schoolyard, measuring 3910 fathoms (top. no. 316) 2. house and farmstead No. 110b measuring 2230 fathoms, as well as the associated garden measuring 217 fathoms (top. nos. 309 and 308) 3. the school garden measuring 8510 fathoms (top. no. 49) 4. the land in the "Habesch" now used by the teaching staff, totalling 10 joch. Expressly excepted from this is the arable land below the village, now in the use of the teachers for church services. It measures 1 joch and 13 sq. fathoms (top. no. 727). This land was formerly in the use of the preacher and is still entered in the land register as belonging to the "pastor's assistant". After the abolition of the preacher's post the teaching staff used it, because they also partly took over the preacher's duties. This land must therefore remain with the parish for the same purpose. Whether it trains a lay helper, or a believing teacher performs this service, - it must be paid by the parish, and this plot shall continue to serve for that. Also expressly excepted from the handover are all other assets of the parish. For these assets the parish receives an annual rent at the level paid by the state to the Orthodox Church for similar assets. The rent is to be obtained by the Ethnic Group, in agreement with the Church, from the state or from the civil community. 5. The rent will be used in its entirety to pay off the debts still burdening the school building until these debts are cleared. 6. Payment of all current fees and taxes, as well as maintenance of the buildings, is borne by the German Ethnic Group. 7. The rooms in the school are available to the Church free of charge for services, confirmation classes and other parish needs outside school hours. 8. Insofar as the Ethnic Group needs the premises of the hall for running the school, these are likewise made available free of charge by the parish. 9. Of the cellar rooms of the school building, two are at the unrestricted and free disposal of the parish. 10. The free and unrestricted use of the approach to the church and the hall leading through the schoolyard is guaranteed to the parish. 11. Religious instruction remains a regular school subject in the sense and to the extent of the legal provisions applicable to it. 12. The German Ethnic Group will make possible voluntary church services by the Evangelical school employees. 13. In the event of a later complete handover of the school property to the Ethnic Group, mutual, separate, legally valid contracts are to be concluded. But it is already stated now that in return the parish must at least be enabled to create a suitable building serving its purposes and needs.' The chairman opens the discussion. Rector Lautner states: The chairman's remarks bear witness to thorough work, and it is good that they can also be found in the archive for later times. But this does not concern us now. The settling of individual questions should be left to the specialist committee. It must now be done as the Ethnic Group leadership demands. That is necessary if only with regard to the state. He supports the motion of Michael Frank 18. The chairman remarks on this: If these things do not concern us as a church body, then they concern no one at all. We have to pass the most far-reaching resolutions, and do so in free self-determination and with unambiguous arrangements. The state could pay the teachers' salaries even now, as is done in Northern Transylvania by the Hungarian state. Rector Lautner states: This concerns property which the Church has administered until now. Now the Ethnic Group is to administer this property. So it always remains ours, for we are after all the same people. The trust we have given the Church until now we now give to the Ethnic Group. The chairman remarks on this: This concerns property which the Church created for itself and which forms its property. That we are unfortunately no longer the same people has been shown by the agitation of the last days, - as also emerges from the remarks made at the beginning. (Two blank pages follow.) Johann Gull 50 speaks in favour of the handover, while churchwarden Klockner recommends acceptance of the chairman's motion. Rector Lautner moves to adjourn this item. The chairman's motion had not been expected and the questions raised in it were unknown. It would also be good to learn how other communities would handle this matter. The chairman opens the motion to adjourn for discussion. Churchwarden Klockner speaks against an adjournment. The chairman remarks on this: churchwarden and local leader Frank had asked him to hold a meeting to deal with this item, and indeed he had to report by 13 December of this year at the latest. Although it had been difficult for the chairman in terms of time, he had called the meeting for today so as not to cause the local leader difficulties with his superior authority. Now the motion to adjourn comes from the same side. Where is German sincerity in that?! As to what the other communities resolve, it is already known that some have resolved one way and others another, and indeed precisely also in the sense of the counter-motion. The vote gives 8 votes in favour, and thus the motion to adjourn this item is accepted." 19 Dec 1941: (Friday) "The chairman reports that 8 members have requested the calling of a meeting to deal with this item again. He recalls that this matter was adjourned at the last meeting and opens the discussion. Churchwarden and local leader Frank points out that the neighbouring communities have already passed resolutions in the sense of his motion and that the Regional Consistory has also recommended it so. The chairman remarks that he too has looked for reasons for the necessity of handing over the property to the Ethnic Group, but has found none. He would be grateful if one were given him here. It is completely incomprehensible to him why this property handover must take place so quickly, i.e. within a few days. Once the bodies had passed resolutions on it, these could no longer be reversed; for the power of disposal over this property in Roseln would then lie outside the community. There would still be time later for handing over the property. - Rector Lautner remarks that in this matter there is no 'against'; what the Regional Consistory and the Ethnic Group say is sacred. Many communities had already resolved in the sense of churchwarden Frank's motion and we should not lag behind. He moves to close the debate. This motion is rejected by 2 votes to 12. - Albrich 63 asks: To whom is the leadership of the Ethnic Group responsible? - The chairman replies: To the people and to the state, as we are told again and again. - As no one else asks to speak, the chairman orders a roll-call vote on the counter-motion. Whoever votes for the motion is to answer 'yes' when his name is called, whoever votes against, 'no'. Voting 'Yes' for the counter-motion: Pastor Lutsch, Curator Fleischer, churchwarden Klockner, Fleischer 66, Geisel 101, Hartel 10. - Voting 'No': churchwarden Frank, Rector Lautner, Balthes 104, Gull 50, Albrich 63, Albrich 76, Stirner 60 and Frank 6. - Thus the counter-motion is rejected by 6 votes to 8. The chairman states that the Frank motion now remains for discussion. On it he makes a 2nd counter-motion with the following content: '1.) The Evangelical parish of Roseln hands over with immediate effect the pedagogical, disciplinary and administrative management of the entire German school and educational system hitherto maintained and managed by it to the German Ethnic Group in Romania, with all the rights and duties arising therefrom. 2.) The Ethnic Group takes over the teaching staff hitherto in the service of the parish of Roseln, preserving their acquired financial rights. 3.) No costs of any kind, nor financial claims of third parties, may accrue to the parish of Roseln as a result of the handover of the school system with all its consequences. For this reason all teaching staff hitherto in its service must resign their posts with the parish upon the handover. The salaries of the teaching staff until 30 March 1942 will be paid by the parish of Roseln according to the instructions to be given by the most worshipful Regional Consistory. 4.) In order to be able to take over the running of the school, the parish of Roseln at the same time hands over to the German Ethnic Group in Romania the following movable and immovable assets forming its property: a.) The movable assets are the furnishings and teaching materials of the school. b.) The immovable assets of the school include 1. The school building built in 1936 together with the teacher's residence and the schoolyard, measuring 341 square fathoms (top. no. 316). 2. House and farmstead No. 110 b measuring 223 square fathoms, as well as the associated garden measuring 217 square fathoms (top. no. 49). 4. The land in the "Habesch" now used by the teaching staff, totalling 10 joch. Expressly excepted from this is the arable land below the village, now in the use of the teachers for church services. It measures 1 joch and 13 square fathoms and has top. no. 727. This land was formerly in the use of the preacher and is still entered in the land register as belonging to the "pastor's assistant". After the abolition of the preacher's post the teaching staff used it, because they also partly took over the preacher's duties. This land must therefore remain with the parish for the same purpose. Whether it trains a lay helper, or a believing teacher performs this service, - it must be paid by the parish, and this plot shall continue to serve for that. Also expressly excepted from the handover are all other assets of the parish. c.) The German Ethnic Group takes over all debts still outstanding from the school building. 5.) The transfer of property rights takes place only after the passing of a corresponding law. 6.) Until the transfer of property rights is carried out, the assets listed under point 4 are at the free and unrestricted disposal of the German Ethnic Group in Romania for school and educational purposes. 7.) Foundations fall entirely outside the above resolution and are not to be handed over even provisionally. 8.) Payment of all current fees and taxes, as well as maintenance of the buildings, is borne by the German Ethnic Group from the day of takeover. 9.) The rooms in the school are available to the Church free of charge for services, confirmation classes and other parish needs outside school hours - until an appropriate new arrangement. 10.) Insofar as the Ethnic Group needs the premises of the hall for running the school, these are likewise made available free of charge by the parish. 11.) Of the cellar rooms of the school building, two are at the unrestricted and free disposal of the parish until the parish has suitable rooms of its own. 12.) The free and unrestricted use of the approach to the church and the hall leading through the schoolyard is guaranteed to the parish without disturbance and for ever. 13.) Religious instruction remains a regular school subject in the sense and to the extent of the legal provisions applicable to it. 14.) The German Ethnic Group makes possible voluntary church services by the Evangelical school employees.' The chairman opens the discussion. Rector Lautner asks to speak and remarks that he does not understand why it must be laid down that the teachers must resign from the church; that goes without saying; and he moves the rejection of this counter-motion and the acceptance of churchwarden Frank's motion. The chairman replies that he knows of a case where a teacher stated in open session: If the Ethnic Group transfers me, I will not go; then my salary will be stopped; then I will remember that I have an employment contract with the parish and will sue it for its fulfilment. -- If such a resignation goes without saying, we would after all be of one mind. It matters everything to him to have unambiguous clarity in the school handover, so that the most unpleasant disputes cannot arise from it. As no one else asks to speak, the chairman has a roll-call vote taken on this counter-motion. Voting 'Yes' for the chairman's motion: Curator Fleischer, churchwarden Klockner, Fleischer 66, Geisel 101, Frank 6, Hartel 10 and Pastor Lutsch. Voting 'No' against the motion: churchwarden Frank, Rector Lautner, Balthes 104, Gull 50, Albrich 63, Albrich 76 and Stirner 60. The chairman states that with the present voting result of 7 to 7, the counter-motion has been accepted and adopted as a resolution in accordance with point 6 of paragraph 9 of the Church Order. A further vote on churchwarden Frank's motion is therefore unnecessary." Finally it is also resolved unanimously to convene the community representation for Sunday, 21 December 1941, at 7 o'clock in the evening. 28 Dec 1941: "Handover of the elementary school with its movable and immovable property to the German Ethnic Group in Romania." "Before proceeding to the agenda, the chairman reports that the minutes of the last meeting are not available, because he did not have time to prepare them and the parish now has no secretary. On the agenda he remarks that 7 members have applied in writing for a meeting to be called to deal with this item. - Rector Lautner asks to speak and states: The presbytery's motion from the previous meeting was rejected by the community representation. It is necessary that this matter be brought to a conclusion here too, since only three communities in the district are still holding back. - Churchwarden and local leader Frank makes the following motion: '1. To transfer into the ownership of the German Ethnic Group in Romania, free of charge, the schools and educational institutions maintained and managed by the parish of Roseln with all associated movable and immovable assets. The individual assets are to be determined and assigned by a specialist committee to which, besides the representatives of the Ethnic Group and the Regional Church, a representative of our parish also belongs. 2. Until the transfer of property rights in the above assets on the basis of the resolution once it has become legally binding, these assets are to be placed at the disposal of the German Ethnic Group in Romania immediately, free of charge and without restriction, and the educational, disciplinary and administrative management of the local schools and educational institutions handed over to the school office of the German Ethnic Group in Romania. This in confident expectation of subsequent approval by the higher authority. 3. The rooms in schools and educational institutions to be handed over to the German Ethnic Group in Romania are available to the parish free of charge for services in justified cases, for confirmation classes and other parish needs outside school hours, until an appropriate new arrangement. 4. No costs or claims of third parties of any kind whatsoever may accrue to the parish from the implementation of these resolutions. The treasury or the school office of the German Ethnic Group in Romania must take over the active and retired teaching staff hitherto in the service of the parish and the active and retired administrative officials thereby released, preserving their acquired financial rights.' The chairman opens the discussion. He himself remarks that he rejects this motion, because it brings no unambiguous clarification of the matter. Also, by accepting it, the parish gives up the right to decide on its property itself. Furthermore, most of the points issued as instructions by the most worshipful Regional Consistory are missing from it. Rector Lautner states: All communities have resolved this motion, and so we should not do anything different. There is no sense in the Church and the Ethnic Group leadership mistrusting each other. - The chairman remarks on this that it is also incomprehensible to him why the Church, which until now has done no less than everything for the school, is so mistrusted that such a blank cheque is demanded of it. Moreover, it is not true that all communities have resolved this motion; it is known of many communities that they have passed resolutions deviating more or less from it. - As no one else asks to speak, the chairman orders a roll-call vote, pointing to para. 9 point 7 of the Church Order, according to which this concerns the rescinding of a resolution already passed by the presbytery in this matter. (PP 20/82) Telefongespräch mit der Tochter am 6.6.2006: Der Vater kehrte im Herbst 1945 heim, aus Russland entlassen, in SS-Uniform, da er keine anderen Kleider hatte, er verbarg sie unter einer umgehängten Decke. Daheim durfte er sich nicht melden, sondern musste sich verstecken. Sie waren mehrere: Johann Widmann, Adjuvantenleiter, Johann Widmann neben Töpfer, Friedrich Rochus aus der Obergasse. Meist versteckte er sich bei seiner Schwester in der Obergasse. Im "Ruide Land" hatten sie einen Garten, in dem sie einen Bunker aushoben, mit grasbewchsener Erde bedeckten, wo sie sich auch im Winter versteckten und wohnten. In der Osternacht 1948 (?) wurde er gefangengenommen und nach Schäßburg geführt. Dort konnte er sich freikaufen (Bestechung) und kam heim. Januar 1949 fuhr er nach Bukarest auf Arbeit. Dort war man unbekannt, nicht verfolgt. Er nahm auch Frau und die beiden mittleren Töchter, Sofia und Katharina, mit. Die beiden Töchter kamen im Herbst wieder heim. Die Eltern blieben bis 1951. Dann kamen sie heim und er ließ sich bei der Staatswirtschaft anstellen. Von dort ging er weg und trat in die Kollektivwirtschaft ein, bei der er bis zur Auswanderung verblieb. 02.05.1948: 29. At home he was not allowed to register, but had to hide. There were several of them: Johann Widmann, leader of the adjuvants [church band], Johann Widmann next to Töpfer, Friedrich Rochus from the Obergasse. Mostly he hid at his sister's in the Obergasse. notes: 24.01.1937: „Gleich zu Beginn der Sitzung fordert der Vorsitzende Herrn Richter Rochus und die beiden Knechtsväter auf, einen genauen Tatsachenbericht über den Verlauf des Jugendballes am 3. Christtag zu erstatten, nachdem ihm beschämende Begebenheiten, die sich damals zugetragen hatten, zur Kenntnis gebracht worden seien. - Es meldet sich zunächst Herr Richter Rochus zu Wort und berichtet, dass er wohl die ausgeschlossenen Burschen zunächst aufgefordert habe, nicht zu tanzen. - Die Burschen hatten sich auch seiner und der Aufforderung der Knechtväter gefügt. - Am Abend jedoch seien die aus der Jugend ausgeschlossenen Burschen wieder zum Tanz erschienen und zwar mit einer Gruppe junger Männer, die die Burschen aufgehetzt hatten zu tanzen, ja sie sogar in den Reihen geschoben hätten. - Eine Aufforderung zum Abtreten sei fruchtlos geblieben; nachdem er nun die Mädchen aufgefordert habe, mit den aus der Jugend ausgeschlossenen Burschen nicht mehr zu tanzen, widrigenfalls sie den Saal verlassen und 20 Lei Strafen zahlen müssten, wären die Männer und auch Frauen in heftige Erregung geraten, die sich für das Bleiben der Ausgeschlossenen eingesetzt hätten. - Die weiteren Anordnungen hatten nicht mehr geholfen, sie wären von der Gruppe Männer niedergeschrieen worden, die auch zu erkennen gegeben hätten, lieber auf eine Schlägerei ankommen zu lassen, als sich der Ordnung zu fügen. - Bei weiteren Erklärungen des Knechtsvaters Albrich 63 wird festgestellt, dass der Haupträdelsführer bei der ganzen Sache das Gemeindevertretungsmitglied Michael Rochus 95, der die Aufhetzung organisiert und angeführt habe, gewesen sei. - In seinen Beschimpfungen sei er soweit gegangen, dass er dort gesagt hätte: Die Presbyter seien Drecksäcke! In beschämender und herausfordernder Weise taten sich auch die jungen Männer vor: Michael Widmann 71; Martin Hermann 72; Martin Rochus 73 und das Gemeindevertretungsmitglied G. Hartel 98.- So hätte das fast vollzählig anwesende Presbyterium allem den freien Lauf lassen müssen. - Nach angeregter Debatte wird auch vor den Presbytern zur Kenntnis gebracht, dass der Presbyter Albrich Martin 117 mitgeteilt habe, dass das Bruderschaftsmitglied Frank Michael 16 an dem Tag nach dem Tanz folgende Äußerung über das Presbyterium getan habe: Na, jetzt haben sich die Presbyter blamiert, nichts haben sie schaffen können, sie sind wert, dass man sie alle an die Wand stellt und anbrunst. - Angesichts dieser beschämenden Vorfälle beschließt das Presbyterium nach gründlicher Beratung, diesen Tatsachenbestand dem Bezirkskonsistorium zu berichten und es zu ersuchen energisch einzuschreiten und die Schuldigen hart zu bestrafen, damit für die Zukunft solch beschämende Vorfälle ausgeschlossen sind. Über eine etwaige Anzeige beim Bezirksgericht wegen Amtsehrenbeleidigung soll vorerst die Stellungnahme der vorgesetzten Behörde dazu ersucht werden. - Nach diesem gefassten Beschluss entspinnt sich eine weitere Aussprache betreff dieser Angelegenheit, in der sich herausstellt, dass einer in dieser Sitzung anwesende Presbyter unter jene Gruppe zu Gewalttat geneigten Männer erklärt habe, dass er selbst im Presbyterium den Antrag gestellt habe, die Ausgeschlossenen tanzen zu lassen, aber die anderen Presbyter hatten nicht auf ihn gehört, sie wären an diesem Schuld. Nach dem die vergebliche Aufforderung an diesen Presbyter ergeht sich zu melden, erklärt Vorsitzender auch dieses zu Anzeige zu bringen.“ 17.03.1937: Rochus 95 ist bereit die Spesen der Voruntersuchung zu tragen und das Presbyterium um Verzeihung zu bitten. Es stellt sich heraus, dass seit der Ehrenbeleidigung von Frank 16 mehr als 3 Monate vergangen sind. Dr. Kirtscher warnt vor einer Klage. Auch vor gerichtlichen Schritten gegen Höchsmann 121 warnt er. So wird ihm verboten 1 Jahr lang den Saal zu betreten. 16.12.1937. b) Nachdem einige Mitglieder des Presbyteriums eine geradezu gemeine Begebenheit gelegentlich einer Zusammenkunft der Jugend dem Presbyterium unterbreiten, jedoch nicht den Tatsachenbestand im Einzelnen wissen, wird Altknecht Albert zur Sitzung gerufen, der berichtet, dass die Burschen Frank Michael 16 und Andreas Höchsmann 90 sich in der Rockenstube bei Herrn Albrich 76 gemein und unsittlich benommen hätten, indem sie vor der Schwester- und Bruderschaft trotz Zurechtweisung mit einem Präservativ die unverschämsten Stückchen vorgeführt hätten. - Das Presbyterium nimmt den Bericht von Altknecht Albert mit vollster Entrüstung zur Kenntnis und beschließt einstimmig, dass die beiden Knechtsväter sofort diesen Tatsachenbestand telefonisch Herrn Stuhlrichter zur Anzeige bringen sollen, um gegen die beiden Genannten strengste Maßnahmen zu ergreifen. Andreas Höchsmann 90, der schon öfters ein ungesittetes Benehmen gezeigt hat, wird weiterhin verboten, von dem heutigen Tage an, mit der Jugend irgendwie in Verbindung zu stehen; Frank Michael 16 darf auch bis dahin in keiner Weise mit der Jugend in Verbindung stehen, bis nicht vom Presbyterium aus festgestellt wird, dass er sich gebessert hat.“

24 Jan 1937: "At the very start of the meeting the chairman asks the judge, Mr Rochus, and the two brotherhood fathers to give an exact account of what happened at the youth ball on the third day of Christmas, since shameful incidents that took place there had been brought to his notice. Judge Rochus speaks first and reports that he had at first asked the expelled young men not to dance, and that they had complied with his request and that of the brotherhood fathers. In the evening, however, the young men who had been expelled from the youth came back to the dance, together with a group of young married men who had egged them on to dance and even pushed them into the line. A request to leave had no effect. When he then told the girls not to dance any more with the expelled young men, or else they would have to leave the hall and pay a fine of 20 lei, the men and also women who were standing up for the expelled young men became extremely agitated. Further orders did no good; they were shouted down by the group of men, who also made it clear that they would rather risk a fight than submit to order. From further statements by brotherhood father Albrich No. 63 it is established that the chief ringleader in the whole affair was the parish assembly member Michael Rochus No. 95, who had organised and led the incitement. In his abuse he went so far as to say there that the presbyters were 'scumbags'! The young married men Michael Widmann No. 71, Martin Hermann No. 72, Martin Rochus No. 73 and the parish assembly member G. Hartel No. 98 also behaved in a shameful and provocative way. And so the presbytery, almost all of whom were present, had to let everything take its course. After lively debate the presbyters are also told that presbyter Martin Albrich No. 117 has reported that the brotherhood member Michael Frank No. 16 said the following about the presbytery on the day after the dance: 'Well, now the presbyters have made fools of themselves, they couldn't do a thing, they deserve to be put up against the wall and pissed on.' In view of these shameful incidents the presbytery decides, after thorough discussion, to report these facts to the district consistory and ask it to intervene firmly and punish the guilty severely, so that such shameful incidents are ruled out in future. As to a possible complaint to the district court for insulting officials, the view of the superior authority is to be sought first. After this decision a further discussion of the matter develops, in which it emerges that one of the presbyters present at this meeting had declared among that group of men inclined to violence that he himself had moved in the presbytery to let the expelled young men dance, but the other presbyters had not listened to him and were to blame. When the request to this presbyter to come forward goes unanswered, the chairman declares that he will report this too." 17 Mar 1937: Rochus 95 is willing to bear the costs of the preliminary investigation and to ask the presbytery's forgiveness. It turns out that more than 3 months have passed since the defamation of Frank 16. Dr. Kirtscher warns against a lawsuit. He also warns against legal steps against Höchsmann 121. So he is forbidden to enter the hall for 1 year. 16 Dec 1937 (b): "Since some members of the presbytery have reported a downright vile incident at a gathering of the young people, but do not know the facts in detail, the senior brotherhood officer (Altknecht) Albert is called to the meeting. He reports that the young men Michael Frank No. 16 and Andreas Höchsmann No. 90 behaved vilely and indecently in the spinning room at Mr Albrich's (No. 76), performing the most shameless tricks with a condom in front of the sisterhood and brotherhood despite being reprimanded. The presbytery receives Altknecht Albert's report with the utmost indignation and decides unanimously that the two brotherhood fathers shall at once report these facts by telephone to the district judge, so that the strictest measures are taken against the two. Andreas Höchsmann No. 90, who has often behaved improperly before, is forbidden from today on to have any contact with the young people; Michael Frank No. 16 may likewise have no contact with them until the presbytery is satisfied that he has mended his ways."

"There is a petition from the local preacher-teacher for the installation of a tiled stove with heating box in place of the previous cast-iron stove. - Resolution: After long and thorough discussion the petition is granted, but on condition that this is the last change in the stove saga, and if this stove too should not suffice, the preacher concerned is to have a stove that suits him installed at his own expense." Moved to Felldorf. Item 41/1899: G. Widmann senior, retired teacher (?), confirms the withdrawal of all application documents of his son Georg Widmann, school rector in Sz. Sáros, for the local preacher-teacher post. The parish office reports this occurrence to the district consistory and asks whether it is permissible to elect the applicant Johann Friedrich as preacher-teacher without a new competition. The community representation is resolved to do so unanimously. 9 Mar 1899. 03 Apr 1899: Item 39. Since the district dean has given his consent that one of the previous applicants may be elected without a new competition, and since both applicants are still willing to accept election, the community representation is recommended to elect Johann Friedrich, rector in Maldorf. 23 Apr 1899. Item 62. Preacher-teacher Friedrich has signed the contract (concerning the preacher's land). The churchwardens are to cultivate the parcels for him. 14 May 1899. Item 73. On Whit Monday preacher-teacher Johann Friedrich will deliver his inaugural sermon. Item 74/899: Joh. Friedrich, rector, Maldorf, 19 Apr 1899 writes: the request to submit his baptismal certificate and a sermon came unexpectedly from Gustav Schullerus, Großschenk. It has been done. He had rather expected confirmation of the election. He mentions the salary certificate, which is missing, but everything may be in order. The subject of the tree nursery is delicate. He cannot leave Maldorf, since in case of a death the adjuvants are unreliable. Then there would be a storm. Hence the proposal: move on Monday or at the latest Tuesday. The day before, the wagons would have to be in Maldorf to be loaded. Item 199/99: Johann Friedrich asks to be given a dwelling within 24 hours, since for 6 weeks he has asked the presbytery in vain to make the dwelling habitable for him. PP 97/97: Item 8 Ordination costs: churchwarden Geisel presents the bill for the costs of the ordination of preacher Friedrich, according to which he charges 12 florins 43 kreuzer in allowances for 4 days, 5 florins cartage and 6 florins for sugar and coffee. - Resolution: The presbytery grants 20 florins all in all." PP 97/263, 07 Jan 1906: Item 1 "The chairman greets those present and opens the meeting with the announcement that preacher-teacher Johann Friedrich, elected to the second teaching post in Felldorf, has applied for his release from the service of this church and school. Regarding his move, Johann Friedrich has told him orally that he will travel by rail to Schäßburg on Thursday 11 January at 5 o'clock in the morning and from there set out by wagon for his new home. He regrets that, because of complete darkness at the time of his departure, no public farewell can be given to the departing teacher. But so that the presbytery may nevertheless take leave of the teacher in a fitting manner, he proposes: the presbytery should assemble in the parish office room on the eve of the move, i.e. on 10 January at 7 o'clock in the evening, and from there pay the preacher-teacher a farewell visit as a body, at which the curator, after introductory words from the pastor, will give the farewell speech. Those present agree to the motion and it is resolved: preacher-teacher Johann Friedrich shall be granted the requested release from the service of this church and school, with an expression of thanks for his fruitful work. On 10 January the presbytery meets in the parish office room, from where it goes to the preacher-teacher's dwelling to take leave, and the pastor and curator address words of thanks to the departing teacher."

According to report item 19-2.1945 on LKZ.3264/1944 of 30 June 1945, Emma Gärtner was at that time employed as provisional teacher and Hildegard Gunne as supplementary teacher. It is reported that the apologetics courses referred to in point a on page 4 of the decree concerned have been running for about 4 weeks for 2 to 2 ½ hours weekly; "they will be completed in about 2 weeks. The course follows the booklet by former Bishop Glondys, which had been sent to us for this purpose. The two teachers named do not attempt to contradict the material and the dogma of our Church, but they have not yet attained a living Evangelical life of faith." R226 "Of the grain in stock the widow takes the 11 Kübel of corn she brought in, 17 Kübel of maize, then from what is to be divided 2 Kübel of the same, 2 and ¾ Kübel of maize, and 4 and ¾ Kübel of rye. The children each receive 4 Kübel of corn, 5 Kübel of maize, 1 Kübel and 12 measures of rye, then ¼ hemp seed, 1 and ½ quarters of beans and 1 Kübel of oats. After the harvest the grain is divided into 2 parts, because according to the contract the widow takes half of what was sown; the other half the children divide among themselves. Of the finished hemp in stock the children jointly receive 1 Creutz and 25 lb; from this the contribution of Rhenish florins 11 kreuzer 30 W.W. is to be paid, the rest to be divided jointly. Of the boards in stock the children receive 11 pieces at 18 kreuzer …. Of the expensive purchased wood the widow receives half, i.e. 5 Rhenish florins W.W. Of the roof tiles in stock the widow receives half; the other half the siblings give to Michael. That this was carried out by the undersigned according to their best judgement and conscientiously is hereby confirmed at Roseln, 4 May 1848. Presbytery minutes 24 Nov 1889: The church musicians Martin Geisel and Michael Buchholzer are each granted 2 florins salary for 1878.

Re-elected on 4.9.1898 with 9 votes. PP 97/101 item 19. PP 97/164 06.11.1901 re-elected as junior churchwarden.

Z.17 Kirchenväter hätten das Heu zu billig verkauft. Sollen zur Verantwortung gezogen werden. Z.18 Vier Presbyter (Martin Fleischer, Martin Geisel, Johann Buchholzer und Johann Zucker) treten aus Presbyterium aus weil Kirchenheu um 20 fl. zu billig verkauft wurde. 12.03.93: 3 Seiten wegen des verkauften Heu. Die Kirchenväter erklären sich bereit, aus ihrer Tasche zu bezahlen, was beschlossen wird. Das Presbyterium beschließt einstimmig, dass sie nichts zu bezahlen haben. 19.03.93: Prüfungstermin wird festgesetzt. Prüfungskommissär soll aus Agnetheln abgeholt werden. Z.26 Die vier Presbyter sind endgültig ausgetreten. Da für solchen Fall nichts vorgesehen ist, soll beim Bezirksdekanat angefragt werden, wie man sich verhalten soll. Z.27 Von Erstklässern sind die Sabbathalien eingehoben bzw. zu Kirchenvater Häner gebracht werden. 24.01.1900. Z.8 Ordinationskosten: Kirchenvater Geisel legt vor die Rechnung über die Kosten der Ordination des Predigers Friedrich, darnach verrechnet er 12 fl. 43 kr. an Diäten auf 4 Tage 5 fl. Fuhrlohn und 6 fl. für Zucker und Kaffee. - Beschluss: Das Presbyterium bewilligt alle in allem 20 fl.“ Z.9 Beschluss „Die Ausgabe von 2 fl. 15 kr. für Fleisch gelegentlich der Übersiedlung des Pfarrers Heltmann wird ebenfalls bewilligt.“ 06.02.1900: Winkler Nachbarschaft beschwert sich, dass die ältesten Mitglieder der Nachbarschaft: Martin Geisel und Johann Buchholzer Kirchenväter, sowie Martin Buchholzer Organist nicht unter Kandidaten aufgenommen wurden. Vorsitzer begründet, die Kirchenväter seien vollauf beschäftigt, da Neubau des Predigerhofes bevorstehe, der Organist besitze das Freitum. 06.11.1901. Z.82 Wahl der Kirchenväter Andreas Hartel Nr.106 zum älteren (war doch Kurator bis wann?) und Geisel 101 zum jüngeren wieder gewählt. 15.12.1909. Schulbrunnen wieder reparaturbedürftig. Benutzer denken nicht an Wiederherstellung. So soll er auf Kosten der Kirchenkasse repariert werden. Alle die sich mit Wasser von ihm bedienen, haben jährlich eine Benützungstaxe von 5 K zu zahlen. Das Tränken des Viehs beim Brunnen ist unter keinen Umständen gestattet. Auch das Waschen ist durchaus nicht erlaubt. Von diesen Einschränkungen sind nur der Pfarrer, Rektor, Lehrer (Lehrerin) befreit. Die Kontrolle hierüber übernimmt Martin Geisel 101.

Item 17: The churchwardens are said to have sold the hay too cheaply. They are to be held to account. Item 18: Four presbyters (Martin Fleischer, Martin Geisel, Johann Buchholzer and Johann Zucker) leave the presbytery because the church hay was sold 20 florins too cheaply. 12 Mar 1893: 3 pages about the hay sold. The churchwardens declare themselves willing to pay out of their own pockets, which is decided. The presbytery decides unanimously that they have nothing to pay. 19 Mar 1893: The examination date is fixed. The examination commissioner is to be fetched from Agnetheln. Item 26: The four presbyters have left for good. Since no provision exists for such a case, the district deanery is to be asked how to proceed. Item 27: The Sabbath dues (Sabbathalien) have been collected from the first-years or are to be taken to churchwarden Häner. Item 38: Johann Buchholzer No. 92 has declared his resignation from the presbytery in the presence of curator Andreas Hartel and churchwarden Michael Häner. The seat is to stay vacant until the next parish assembly. 24.01.1900. Item 8, ordination costs: Churchwarden Geisel presents the account of the costs of the ordination of the preacher Friedrich, according to which he charges 12 fl. 43 kr. in daily allowances for 4 days, 5 fl. carriage fee and 6 fl. for sugar and coffee. - Resolution: The presbytery approves 20 fl. in all." Item 9, resolution: "The expenditure of 2 fl. 15 kr. for meat on the occasion of the moving-in of Pastor Heltmann is likewise approved." 6 Feb 1900: The Winkel neighbourhood complains that its oldest members, Martin Geisel and Johann Buchholzer, churchwardens, and Martin Buchholzer, organist, were not included among the candidates. The chairman explains that the churchwardens are fully occupied, since the rebuilding of the preacher's house is imminent, and that the organist is exempt. 06.11.1901. Item 82, election of the churchwardens: Andreas Hartel No. 106 re-elected as senior (was he not curator until when?) and Geisel 101 as junior. 15.12.1909. The school well is again in need of repair. The users give no thought to restoring it. So it is to be repaired at the expense of the church fund. All who draw water from it are to pay an annual usage fee of 5 crowns. Watering livestock at the well is not permitted under any circumstances. Washing is likewise strictly forbidden. Only the pastor, rector and teacher (female teacher) are exempt from these restrictions. Martin Geisel 101 takes over the supervision of this.

07.05.1909: Gemäß Verabredung soll Übersiedlung der beiden Lehrer am 10. Mai stattfinden. Beschluss: „Die Wägen sollen so fahren, dass zwölf davon am 9 d. Mts früh um 7 Uhr in Schönberg und drei um dieselbe Zeit in Agnetheln sind. Jeder Wagen soll wo möglich auch ein wenig Stroh mitnehmen. Für Sonntag sind dann zwei Vierergespänne zu bestellen, von denen das eine nach Schönberg, das andere nach Agnetheln fährt um die neu gewählten Lehrer abzuholen. Die Kirchenväter fahren auch mit. Hinsichtlich der Ankunft haben sie die Abfahrt so einzurichten, dass die Wägen mit den Lehrern pünktlich um 3 Uhr nachmittags bei unserer Mühle eintreffen und dann zusammen hereinfahren. Ein Presbyter reitet mit den Burschen mit und sorgt für Aufrechthaltung der Ordnung und begrüßt die Lehrer beim Zusammentreffen der Burschen mit ihnen. Der Empfang ist still, d. h. ohne Musik, weil die Adjuvanten bis zur Ankunft der Lehrer keinen Marsch einüben können. Der Empfang geschieht in der gewohnten Weise. Am Ende der Gemeinde erwartet das Presbyterium mit dem Kurator an der Spitze die Lehrer und dieser begrüßt sie in einer kurzen Ansprache. Darauf schließt sich das Presbyterium an den Zug an und kommt zur Schule, wo der Pfarrer die beiden Lehrer im Namen der Gemeinde, der Kinder und s. w. begrüßt. Nachher versammelt sich das Presbyterium samt den Lehrer und den zwei sie abholenden Fuhrleuten zu einem gemeinsamen Empfangsmahle dessen Vorbereitung unter Mitwirkung der Pfarrerin und der Notärin von den folgenden Frauen besorgt werden möge. Sofia Salmen, Kuratorin, Anna Frank, Kirchenmutter, Katharina Denndorf, Kirchenmutter, Anna Geisel Nr.101, Anna Zucker Nr.88, Maria Balthes Nr.104. Das Essen findet am zweckmäßigsten im großen Zimmer der Lehrerwohnung statt.“

7 May 1909: As agreed, the two teachers are to move on 10 May. Decision: "The wagons are to go so that twelve of them are in Schönberg at 7 a.m. on the 9th of this month and three in Agnetheln at the same time. Each wagon should also take a little straw if possible. For Sunday two four-horse teams are to be ordered, one going to Schönberg and the other to Agnetheln to fetch the newly elected teachers. The churchwardens go along too. They are to time their departure so that the wagons with the teachers arrive at our mill punctually at 3 p.m. and then drive in together. A presbyter is to ride with the young men to keep order and to greet the teachers when the young men meet them. The welcome is to be quiet, that is, without music, because the church musicians cannot practise a march before the teachers arrive. The welcome takes place in the usual way. At the edge of the village the presbytery, led by the curator, awaits the teachers, and he greets them with a short address. The presbytery then joins the procession to the school, where the pastor welcomes the two teachers in the name of the parish, the children and so on. Afterwards the presbytery, with the teachers and the two carters who fetched them, gathers for a welcome meal, to be prepared, with the help of the pastor's wife and the notary's wife, by the following women: Sofia Salmen, the curator's wife; Anna Frank, churchwarden's wife; Katharina Denndorf, churchwarden's wife; Anna Geisel No. 101; Anna Zucker No. 88; Maria Balthes No. 104. The meal is best held in the big room of the teachers' house."

2620.title: 25 Nov 1917 churchwarden, Roseln (Junior churchwarden, cash box B), church curator, Roseln, church elder (presbyter), Roseln
notes: Jüngerer Kirchenvater Kassa B
Junior churchwarden, fund B

21.01.1906. Z.4 Verkauf des Pfarrers- und Kirchenweingartens im Honfeld. „Martin Geisel Nr.101 hat beim Pfarrer angemeldet, dass er den völlig nutzlosen und schon seit vielen Jahren wüsten Pfarrer- und Kirchenweingarten im Honfeld kaufen wolle, weil beide Parzellen in der daselbst von ihm durch Ankauf aller wüsten Weingärten gemachten Hutweide liegen. Weil weder die Kirche noch der Pfarrer von diesen Parzellen auch nicht den geringsten Nutzen haben, ihm aber bei der freien Ausnützung seine Hutweide unter Umständen hinderlich sein könnten, so bittet der Oben genannte: man möge ihm die beiden Parzellen in einem angemessenen Preise verkaufen. Nach eingehender Beratung kommt der Beschluss zustande: Das Presbyterium willigt in den Verkauf der beiden Weingartenparzellen ein, und zwar soll der Kaufliebhaber für den Pfarrweingarten als den bessern und größeren von beiden 40 Kronen, welche zu Gunsten des Pfarrers nutzbringend angelegt werden sollen - und für den Kirchenweingarten, der eigentlich nutzlos ist 3 Kronen zahlen. Pres.Prot.28.11.1926 (17/98): Thomas Geisel 101 und Töpfer 94 sind im Vermögensstand gleich. "Keiner könne von beiden sagen er wäre im Verhältnis zum andern zu hoch besteuert." 26.04.1924: 29. Presbyterium „möge den Kostenvoranschlag für den Saalbau unabgeändert der Gemeindevertretung zur Beschlussfassung“ vorlegen. Dies wird beschlossen. Wegen Abkleidung des Gebäudes, da im Rekurs nur um dessen oberen Teil gestritten wird, wird beschlossen - auf Antrag Thomas Albrich - gleich nach den Frühjahrsarbeiten damit zu beginnen. Es soll beschlossen werden in welcher Art das Geld für den Saalbau aufzubringen ist. „Kurator Frank stellt den Antrag es solle nach dem alten Schlüssel eingehoben werden. Thomas Geisel 101 stellt den Antrag es solle der Betrag unter alle Bürger gleichmäßig verteilt werden, Witwen und Witwer sollen nur die Hälfte zahlen. Michael Hartel 107 stellt den Antrag es sollten 2/3 des Betrages gleichmäßig 1/3 aber solle nach einem andern Schlüssel aufgeteilt werden. - Alle drei Anträge gelangen zur Abstimmung: Der Antrag Geisel wird mit Stimmenmehrheit angenommen und beschlossen. 14.02.1925. 17. „Der Vorsitzer führt aus, weil in der vorigen Sitzung niemand etwas von einem Essen für den neuen Rektor gesprochen, habe er die Bemerkung gemacht, er wolle den Rektor und seine Familie nach dem Empfang zu sich einladen. Alles hätte dazu geschwiegen. Nun habe er aber erfahren, dass das vielen nicht recht sei, die ein größeres gemeinsames Essen geben wollten. Er sei damit durchaus einverstanden, zumal auch der Empfang des Rektors dadurch würdiger gestaltet werde. Aber es habe ihn gekränkt, dass man ihm das nicht gleich und nicht direkt gesagt - wir kämen doch zusammen, um uns offen und ehrlich auszusprechen. Im übrigen bitte er um Vorschläge. - Balthes 104 tritt dafür ein, man solle mit Rücksicht auf die leere Kirchenkasse von einem größeren Essen absehen und den Pfarrer den Rektor bewirten lassen. - Geisel 101 beantragt ein gemeinsames Essen für Pfarrer, Rektor und Presbyterium, dessen Kosten die daran teilnehmenden Presbyter zu decken hätten. Der Antrag wird angenommen.“ 07.06.1931. Rektor Lautner macht aufmerksam, dass Geisel 101 seit Kommassation Brunnen auf dem Lehrergrund benützt. Er soll in Kanzlei gerufen werden und dort erklären, dass er kein Recht habe (Servitut). 10.06.1935: Vorsitz Kurator Geisel: Kurator begrüßt, Rektor Lautner liest Zuschrift des Gerichts, „dass der Grund der ev. Kirchengemeinde wegen einer Schuld von rund 11.000 Lei (die wahrscheinlich auf rückständige Staatssteuern entfällt) intabuliert sei.“ Es wird beschlossen „heute eine Sammlung zu veranstalten“ und „die Angelegenheit in Angriff zu nehmen“, „vor allen Dingen dahingehend die Sache zu klären, inwieweit der Staat uns verpflichtet, so eine hohe Summe zu fordern, nachdem sich das Presbyterium gar nicht über die Höhe der Summe im Klaren ist“. Es soll sofort eine Extabulierung von Seiten des Staates in die Wege geleitet werden. 24.01.1937: „Gleich zu Beginn der Sitzung fordert der Vorsitzende Herrn Richter Rochus und die beiden Knechtsväter auf, einen genauen Tatsachenbericht über den Verlauf des Jugendballes am 3. Christtag zu erstatten, nachdem ihm beschämende Begebenheiten, die sich damals zugetragen hatten, zur Kenntnis gebracht worden seien. - Es meldet sich zunächst Herr Richter Rochus zu Wort und berichtet, dass er wohl die ausgeschlossenen Burschen zunächst aufgefordert habe, nicht zu tanzen. - Die Burschen hatten sich auch seiner und der Aufforderung der Knechtväter gefügt. - Am Abend jedoch seien die aus der Jugend ausgeschlossenen Burschen wieder zum Tanz erschienen und zwar mit einer Gruppe junger Männer, die die Burschen aufgehetzt hatten zu tanzen, ja sie sogar in den Reihen geschoben hätten. - Eine Aufforderung zum Abtreten sei fruchtlos geblieben; nachdem er nun die Mädchen aufgefordert habe, mit den aus der Jugend ausgeschlossenen Burschen nicht mehr zu tanzen, widrigenfalls sie den Saal verlassen und 20 Lei Strafen zahlen müssten, wären die Männer und auch Frauen in heftige Erregung geraten, die sich für das Bleiben der Ausgeschlossenen eingesetzt hätten. - Die weiteren Anordnungen hatten nicht mehr geholfen, sie wären von der Gruppe Männer niedergeschrieen worden, die auch zu erkennen gegeben hätten, lieber auf eine Schlägerei ankommen zu lassen, als sich der Ordnung zu fügen. - Bei weiteren Erklärungen des Knechtsvaters Albrich 63 wird festgestellt, dass der Haupträdelsführer bei der ganzen Sache das Gemeindevertretungsmitglied Michael Rochus 95, der die Aufhetzung organisiert und angeführt habe, gewesen sei. - In seinen Beschimpfungen sei er soweit gegangen, dass er dort gesagt hätte: Die Presbyter seien Drecksäcke! In beschämender und herausfordernder Weise taten sich auch die jungen Männer vor: Michael Widmann 71; Martin Hermann 72; Martin Rochus 73 und das Gemeindevertretungsmitglied G. Hartel 98.- So hätte das fast vollzählig anwesende Presbyterium allem den freien Lauf lassen müssen. - Nach angeregter Debatte wird auch vor den Presbytern zur Kenntnis gebracht, dass der Presbyter Albrich Martin 117 mitgeteilt habe, dass das Bruderschaftsmitglied Frank Michael 16 an dem Tag nach dem Tanz folgende Äußerung über das Presbyterium getan habe: Na, jetzt haben sich die Presbyter blamiert, nichts haben sie schaffen können, sie sind wert, dass man sie alle an die Wand stellt und anbrunst. - Angesichts dieser beschämenden Vorfälle beschließt das Presbyterium nach gründlicher Beratung, diesen Tatsachenbestand dem Bezirkskonsistorium zu berichten und es zu ersuchen energisch einzuschreiten und die Schuldigen hart zu bestrafen, damit für die Zukunft solch beschämende Vorfälle ausgeschlossen sind. Über eine etwaige Anzeige beim Bezirksgericht wegen Amtsehrenbeleidigung soll vorerst die Stellungnahme der vorgesetzten Behörde dazu ersucht werden. - Nach diesem gefassten Beschluss entspinnt sich eine weitere Aussprache betreff dieser Angelegenheit, in der sich herausstellt, dass einer in dieser Sitzung anwesende Presbyter unter jene Gruppe zu Gewalttat geneigten Männer erklärt habe, dass er selbst im Presbyterium den Antrag gestellt habe, die Ausgeschlossenen tanzen zu lassen, aber die anderen Presbyter hatten nicht auf ihn gehört, sie wären an diesem Schuld. Nach dem die vergebliche Aufforderung an diesen Presbyter ergeht sich zu melden, erklärt Vorsitzender auch dieses zu Anzeige zu bringen.“ 28.01.1937: „Am Schlusse der Sitzung meldet sich Kurator Geisel zu Wort und gibt dem Presbyterium zur Kenntnis, dass er es gewesen sei, der am Jugendball erklärt habe, dass er dem Presbyterium den Antrag gestellt habe, die Ausgeschlossenen Burschen tanzen zu lassen. Nachdem ihm Vorsitzender in entschiedener Weise sagt, dass sich jeder Einzelne, wenn er auch nicht der Meinung des Presbyteriums ist, dem durch Mehrheit gefassten Beschluss zu fügen hat und sich auch daran zu halten hat, wird die Erklärung von Kurator Geisel zur Kenntnis genommen. Nachdem sich niemand zu Wort meldet, berichtet Vorsitzender, dass es ihm zur Kenntnis gebracht worden sei, dass Herr Richter Rochus in der Winklernachbarschaft am Faschingstag in unmissverständlicher Weise erklärt habe, dass er betreffend dem Beschluss der jungen Männer, beim Jugendball die auf der Seite der ausgeschlossenen Burschen hielten, das Vorgehen des Presbyteriums nicht für richtig halte, also somit gegen die Beschlüsse des Presbyteriums agitiert habe. Widmann 107 und Balthes 104 die erklären, bei dieser Aussage von Herrn Rochus 73 anwesend gewesen zu sein, berichten, dass er gesagt habe, dass die schuldigen Männer verurteilt worden seien, trotzdem sie ihr Vergehen eingesehen und um Verzeihung gebeten hätten usw. In der Aussprache betreff dieser Angelegenheit stellt das Presbyterium mit Befremden die Handlungsweise von Herrn Richter Rochus fest, weil es nicht angeht, gegen schon gefasste Beschlüsse zu agitieren. Es wird beschlossen, ihn in der folgenden Sitzung aufzufordern, sich betreffend dieser Angelegenheit zu rechtfertigen.“ 03.01.1939: „Die drei neugewählten Presbyter Thomas Geisel 101 [bis dahin Kurator!], Johann Gull 50 und Thomas Albrich 63, die bei der Einführung aller neugewählter Presbyter im Gotteshause nicht anwesend waren, werden nunmehr vom Vorsitzenden in feierlichster Weise in ihr verantwortungsvolles Amt eingeführt. Der Vorsitzende erteilt anschließend an Herrn Thomas Geisel 101 auf Grund der Vorschrift über das Verfahren bei Verhängung von Ordnungsstrafen Z.2501/1938 eine Rüge, weil der Genannte nicht aus triftigen Gründen der Einführung im Gotteshaus fernblieb.“ [!] „Vorsitzender begrüßt nun das Presbyterium in seiner neuen Zusammensetzung. Auf das vergangene Jahr rückblickend, betont Vorsitzender, dass sich die Kirchengemeinde endlich im vergangenen Jahr von den Bankschulden freimachen und auch die Kirchengebäude entsprechend hergestellt werden konnte, so dass der Kirchengemeinde auf längere Zeit keine größeren Aufgaben gestellt würden. Nun müsse die noch größere Aufgabe, die sich zum Ziel setze, dass christliche Leben in der Gemeinde zu heben, in Angriff genommen werden. Vorbedingung jedoch, dass auch auf diesem Gebiete Wandel eintrete, sei eine beispielgebende Lebenshaltung aller Presbyter. Mit der Bitte alle Kräfte in den Dienst dieser nun größten Aufgabe zu stellen, wird die eindrucksvolle Ansprache beendet.“ 12.03.1939. „Der Vorsitzer teilt mit, dass die Angelegenheit des für Widmann 91 hinterlegten 593.- Lei nun beigelegt sei, dass sich aber Altkurator Geisel bis zur Beilegung sehr unwürdig und kindisch benommen habe. Er hatte das Geld behoben, wollte aber mit der Abrechnung nichts zu tun haben, ebenso Rektor Lautner, der bei der Behebung dabei war. Nachdem darüber fast ein Jahr verstrichen war, blieb überhaupt keine andre Möglichkeit mehr, als Altkurator Geisel schriftlich zur Regelung der Sache aufzufordern. Sein Benehmen den Kirchenvätern gegenüber, die ihm den Brief brachten war sehr unfein; die Annahme verweigerte er und als der Brief durch die Post ihm zugeschickt wurde, sandte er ihn ungeöffnet durch den Postboten an das Presbyterium wieder zurück. Der Vorsitzende warnt Herrn Geisel zum letzten Mal wegen eines solchen unwürdigen Benehmens mit dem Hinweis darauf, dass bei einem etwaigen Wiederholungsfalle um der Ordnung willen alle gesetzlichen Mittel in Anwendung gebracht werden.“

21.01.1906. Item 4, sale of the pastor's and church vineyard in the Honfeld. "Martin Geisel No. 101 has notified the pastor that he wishes to buy the completely useless pastor's and church vineyard in the Honfeld, which has lain waste for many years, because both parcels lie within the pasture he has made there by buying up all the waste vineyards. Since neither the church nor the pastor has the slightest benefit from these parcels, but they could under certain circumstances hinder him in the free use of his pasture, the above-named asks that the two parcels be sold to him at a reasonable price. After thorough deliberation the resolution is reached: The presbytery consents to the sale of the two vineyard parcels; the prospective buyer is to pay 40 crowns for the pastor's vineyard, as the better and larger of the two, which are to be invested profitably in favour of the pastor, and 3 crowns for the church vineyard, which is actually useless." Presbytery minutes 28.11.1926 (17/98): Thomas Geisel 101 and Töpfer 94 are equal in their property status. "Of neither of the two could one say that he was taxed too highly in relation to the other." 26.04.1924: 29. The presbytery "may submit the cost estimate for the hall construction unaltered to the community council for decision". This is resolved. Regarding the cladding of the building, since in the appeal only its upper part is disputed, it is resolved - on the motion of Thomas Albrich - to begin it immediately after the spring work. It is to be decided in what way the money for the hall construction is to be raised. "Curator Frank moves that it should be levied according to the old key. Thomas Geisel 101 moves that the amount should be divided equally among all burghers, widows and widowers to pay only half. Michael Hartel 107 moves that 2/3 of the amount should be divided equally but 1/3 according to another key. - All three motions are put to the vote: The Geisel motion is adopted and resolved by a majority of votes. 14 Feb 1925, item 17: "The chairman states that, because nobody at the last meeting said anything about a meal for the new rector, he had remarked that he would invite the rector and his family to his house after the welcome. Everyone had kept silent. But now he has learned that many are unhappy with this, wanting to give a larger communal meal. He fully agrees, especially as it will make the rector's welcome more dignified. But it hurt him that he was not told so at once and directly; after all, we meet in order to speak openly and honestly. For the rest, he asks for proposals. Balthes No. 104 argues that, given the empty church funds, a larger meal should be dropped and the pastor left to entertain the rector. Geisel No. 101 moves a communal meal for the pastor, rector and presbytery, its cost to be covered by the presbyters taking part. The motion is adopted." 07.06.1931. Rector Lautner points out that Geisel 101 has been using the well on the teacher's land since the land consolidation. He is to be called to the office and told there that he has no right to it (servitude). 10.06.1935: Chaired by Curator Geisel: The curator welcomes those present; Rector Lautner reads a letter from the court "that the land of the Lutheran church parish has been registered with a lien because of a debt of around 11,000 lei (which probably relates to arrears of state taxes)." It is resolved "to hold a collection today" and "to tackle the matter", "above all to clarify the matter as to how far the state is entitled to demand such a high sum from us, since the presbytery is not at all clear about the amount of the sum". The removal of the lien by the state is to be initiated immediately. 24 Jan 1937: "At the very start of the meeting the chairman asks the judge, Mr Rochus, and the two brotherhood fathers to give an exact account of what happened at the youth ball on the third day of Christmas, since shameful incidents that took place there had been brought to his notice. Judge Rochus speaks first and reports that he had at first asked the expelled young men not to dance, and that they had complied with his request and that of the brotherhood fathers. In the evening, however, the young men who had been expelled from the youth came back to the dance, together with a group of young married men who had egged them on to dance and even pushed them into the line. A request to leave had no effect. When he then told the girls not to dance any more with the expelled young men, or else they would have to leave the hall and pay a fine of 20 lei, the men and also women who were standing up for the expelled young men became extremely agitated. Further orders did no good; they were shouted down by the group of men, who also made it clear that they would rather risk a fight than submit to order. From further statements by brotherhood father Albrich No. 63 it is established that the chief ringleader in the whole affair was the parish assembly member Michael Rochus No. 95, who had organised and led the incitement. In his abuse he went so far as to say there that the presbyters were 'scumbags'! The young married men Michael Widmann No. 71, Martin Hermann No. 72, Martin Rochus No. 73 and the parish assembly member G. Hartel No. 98 also behaved in a shameful and provocative way. And so the presbytery, almost all of whom were present, had to let everything take its course. After lively debate the presbyters are also told that presbyter Martin Albrich No. 117 has reported that the brotherhood member Michael Frank No. 16 said the following about the presbytery on the day after the dance: 'Well, now the presbyters have made fools of themselves, they couldn't do a thing, they deserve to be put up against the wall and pissed on.' In view of these shameful incidents the presbytery decides, after thorough discussion, to report these facts to the district consistory and ask it to intervene firmly and punish the guilty severely, so that such shameful incidents are ruled out in future. As to a possible complaint to the district court for insulting officials, the view of the superior authority is to be sought first. After this decision a further discussion of the matter develops, in which it emerges that one of the presbyters present at this meeting had declared among that group of men inclined to violence that he himself had moved in the presbytery to let the expelled young men dance, but the other presbyters had not listened to him and were to blame. When the request to this presbyter to come forward goes unanswered, the chairman declares that he will report this too." 28 Jan 1937: "At the end of the meeting curator Geisel asks to speak and informs the presbytery that it was he who declared at the youth ball that he had moved in the presbytery to let the expelled young men dance. After the chairman tells him firmly that every individual, even if he does not share the presbytery's view, must submit to and abide by a majority decision, curator Geisel's statement is noted. When nobody else asks to speak, the chairman reports that it has come to his notice that the judge, Mr Rochus, declared unmistakably at the Winkel neighbourhood on Shrove Tuesday that, concerning the decision about the young married men who sided with the expelled young men at the youth ball, he did not consider the presbytery's action right, and so had agitated against the presbytery's decisions. Widmann No. 107 and Balthes No. 104, who state that they were present when Mr Rochus No. 73 said this, report that he said the guilty men had been condemned even though they had seen their wrongdoing and asked forgiveness, and so on. In the discussion the presbytery notes with surprise the conduct of the judge, Mr Rochus, since it is not acceptable to agitate against decisions already made. It is decided to call on him at the next meeting to justify himself in this matter." 3 Jan 1939: "The three newly elected presbyters Thomas Geisel No. 101 [until then curator!], Johann Gull No. 50 and Thomas Albrich No. 63, who were not present at the installation of all the newly elected presbyters in church, are now solemnly installed in their responsible office by the chairman. The chairman then, under the regulation on disciplinary penalties no. 2501/1938, reprimands Mr Thomas Geisel No. 101, because he stayed away from the installation in church without good reason." [!] "The chairman now welcomes the presbytery in its new membership. Looking back on the past year, he stresses that last year the parish was at last freed of its bank debts and the church buildings could be properly restored, so that the parish will face no major tasks for some time. Now the even greater task must be tackled: raising the Christian life of the parish. A precondition for change in this area too is an exemplary way of life by all presbyters. The impressive address ends with the request that all put their strength into this greatest task." 12.03.1939. "The chairman reports that the matter of the 593 lei deposited for Widmann 91 has now been settled, but that former curator Geisel behaved in a very undignified and childish manner until it was settled. He had withdrawn the money but wanted nothing to do with the accounting, nor did Rector Lautner, who was present at the withdrawal. After almost a year had passed over this, there was no other option left but to call upon former curator Geisel in writing to settle the matter. His behaviour towards the churchwardens who brought him the letter was very ill-mannered; he refused to accept it, and when the letter was sent to him by post, he sent it back unopened to the presbytery via the postman. The chairman warns Mr Geisel for the last time about such undignified behaviour, pointing out that in any case of repetition all legal means will be applied for the sake of order."

2628.title: churchwarden, Roseln, member of the village council, Roseln
notes: Gemeindevertretung wurden gewählt, für die Zeitdauer von 6 Jahren:
Village council elected for a term of 6 years:

02.04.1944. Neuwahl der Kirchenväter. § 39, 40, 41 und 42 der KO werden verlesen. Alle drei Ämter (Kirchenväter. Älteste und Armenpfleger) werden zusammengelegt, da Kirchenväter nun von Rechnung frei sind, die von Kurator und Pfarrer geführt werden. Bei der Wahl erhalten Martin Widmann 107 12 Stimmen und Michael Geisel Nr.3 7 Stimmen. Diese sind also gewählt. 13.03.1949: 10. „Nach Eröffnung der Sitzung weist der Vorsitzer auf den ungenügenden Taxeneingang hin. Geisel 3 erklärt, nicht mehr einsammeln zu wollen, weil ihm zu viele Grobheiten gesagt würden, und legt seine Stelle nieder. Das Presbyterium nimmt das zur Kenntnis und beauftragt den Kirchenvater Höchsmann mit der Taxeneinhebung im Geiselschen Abschnitt.“

02.04.1944. New election of churchwardens. §§ 39, 40, 41 and 42 of the church ordinance are read out. All three offices (churchwardens, elders and poor-relief officers) are combined, since the churchwardens are now free of accounting, which is kept by the curator and pastor. In the election Martin Widmann 107 receives 12 votes and Michael Geisel No. 3 7 votes. These are therefore elected. 13.03.1949: 10. "After the opening of the meeting the chairman points to the insufficient receipt of fees. Geisel 3 declares that he no longer wishes to collect, because too many rude things are said to him, and resigns his post. The presbytery takes note of this and charges Churchwarden Höchsmann with collecting the fees in Geisel's section."

Hausnummer 3:: Geisel Michael, seine Frau eine geborene Hartel, aus einem ganz anderen Holz geschnitzt, mit dem Dorfhamen Staifen, das Haus etwas von der Gassenfront zurückgesetzt, ein kleines Blumengärtchen vor dem Haus. Eine Bauernfamilie, fleißige und bescheidene Menschen, aber helle in jeder Beziehung. Der Vater ein gediegener gemütlicher Mann mit einem trockenen Humor, der besonders bei Karnevalsveranstaltungen zum Ausdruck kam, hatte seinen Bauernhof immer gut im Schuß und galt im Dorf als Frühaufsteher. Seine Frau, sehr musikalisch, kannte alle Volkslieder und auch alle Strophen sowie die meisten Psalmen auswendig. Wenn die Orgel in der Kirche mal versagte, gab sie den Ton an. Ihr Sohn, der Michael, ganz der Vater, immer bei den Adjuvanten, wo er die Baßtuba blies, kennt jeden aus dem Dorf mit allen Einzelheiten, guten und weniger guten Eigenschaften. Hat einen trockenen Humor, kann auch bei dem besten Witz, auch wenn er unter der Gürtellinie liegt, nie eine Miene verziehen. Mit einem Wort: der geeignetste Mann, den ich mir nach meiner Beurteilung anheuern möchte. Seine Frau, eine geb. Widmann, namens Anna, ist der ruhende Pol. Sie ist die Ruhe selbst, fleißig, sparsam und eine gute Mutter ihrer drei Kinder Renate, Michael und Anneliese. Als eine der letzten Ausgewanderten erzählte sie mir, sie sei einmal durch das Dorf gegangen in dem Bedürfnis, einem Menschen auf sächsisch einen guten Tag zu wünschen, hätte am Dorfende kehrt gemacht und nur mit "buna Ziua", was auf rumänisch "guten Tag " heißt, grüßen können, was sie natürlich sehr mißgestimmt hätte. - Dann waren da noch die beiden Schwestern vom Michael, die Maria, welche bereits in der Geschichte vom Birnenklauen beim rumänischen Pfarrer erwähnt wurde und die Sofia, die das Musikalische von der Mutter geerbt hat, verheiratet mit Schuster Hans, allerdings kein Roseler.

House number 3: Geisel Michael, his wife née Hartel, cut from quite a different cloth, with the village nickname Staifen; the house set back somewhat from the street front, a small flower garden in front of the house. A farming family, hardworking and modest people, but bright in every respect. The father, a solid, easy-going man with a dry humour, which came out especially at carnival events, always kept his farm in good order and was known in the village as an early riser. His wife, very musical, knew all the folk songs, including all the verses, as well as most of the psalms by heart. If the organ in church ever failed, she gave the note. Their son Michael, just like his father, always with the adjuvants [church band], where he played the bass tuba, knows everyone in the village with all the details, good and less good qualities. He has a dry humour and never cracks a smile even at the best joke, even if it is below the belt. In a word: the most suitable man I would want to hire, in my judgement. His wife, née Widmann, named Anna, is the calm centre. She is calmness itself, hardworking, thrifty and a good mother to her three children Renate, Michael and Anneliese. As one of the last to emigrate, she told me she once walked through the village wanting to wish someone a good day in Saxon, turned back at the end of the village and had only been able to greet with "buna Ziua", which means "good day" in Romanian, which of course had greatly upset her. - Then there were also Michael's two sisters, Maria, who was already mentioned in the story of the pear-stealing at the Romanian priest's, and Sofia, who inherited the musicality from her mother, married to Schuster Hans, though not a Roseln man.
